title.zh: 卷一百九十一 列傳第一百十六 忠義上
title.raw: 卷一百九十一 列傳第一百十六 忠義上 Volume 191 Biographies 116: Loyalty and Righteousness 1

sentences.zh: 忠義上

translations.literal: Loyalty and Righteousness, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and Righteousness (Part One)

sentences.zh: 夫有生所甚重者，身也；

translations.literal: Of what one who has life most heavily values, the body is;
translations.idiomatic: Among all things possessed by the living, nothing is valued more heavily than one's own body;

sentences.zh: 得輕用者，忠與義也。

translations.literal: What may be lightly expended are loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Only loyalty and righteousness may be lightly spent.

sentences.zh: 後身先義，仁也；

translations.literal: Placing the body behind and righteousness first is benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: To put righteousness before oneself is benevolence;

sentences.zh: 身可殺，名不可死，誌也。

translations.literal: The body may be killed, but fame may not die — that is resolve.
translations.idiomatic: One's body may be slain, but one's name must not perish — that is true resolve.

sentences.zh: 大凡捐生以趣義者，寧豫期垂名不朽而為之？

translations.literal: Generally those who surrender life to pursue righteousness — would they beforehand plan for immortal lasting fame to do it?
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, would those who give up their lives in pursuit of righteousness do so merely because they expected immortal fame?

sentences.zh: 雖一世成敗，亦未必濟也；

translations.literal: Even the success or failure of a single age may not necessarily be helped;
translations.idiomatic: Even the outcome of an entire age may not necessarily be changed by such acts;

sentences.zh: 要為重所與，終始一操，雖頹嵩、岱，不吾壓也。

translations.literal: The essential point is to honor what one has given oneself to; from beginning to end one holds to a single principle — though Mount Song and Mount Tai may crumble, they cannot press upon me.
translations.idiomatic: What matters is to honor one's commitments and hold to a single principle from start to finish — though even Mount Song and Mount Tai collapse, they cannot weigh upon one.

sentences.zh: 夷、齊排周存商，商不害亡，而周以興。

translations.literal: Bo Yi and Shu Qi opposed Zhou and preserved Shang; Shang's fall was not thereby prevented, yet Zhou rose.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Yi and Shu Qi rejected Zhou and remained loyal to Shang, yet Shang still fell and Zhou still rose.

sentences.zh: 兩人至餓死不肯屈，卒之武王蒙慚德，而夷、齊為得仁，仲尼變色言之，不敢少損焉。

translations.literal: The two men went so far as to starve to death rather than yield; in the end King Wu bore shame for his virtue, while Bo Yi and Shu Qi were held to have attained benevolence — Confucius spoke of it with changed countenance and did not dare diminish it in the least.
translations.idiomatic: The two men starved rather than submit, and in the end King Wu was shamed by his deed while Bo Yi and Shu Qi were judged to have attained true benevolence — Confucius spoke of them with solemn reverence and would not slight them in the least.

sentences.zh: 故忠義者，真天下之大閑歟！

translations.literal: Thus loyalty and righteousness — are they not truly the great barriers of the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Thus loyalty and righteousness are truly the great moral bulwarks of the world!

sentences.zh: 奸鈇逆鼎，搏人而肆其毒，然殺一義士，則四方解情，故亂臣賊子然疑沮而不得逞。

translations.literal: The wicked grind axes and rebel against the tripod, striking men and spreading their poison — yet kill one righteous man and the four quarters lose their hearts; thus rebellious ministers and wicked sons grow suspicious and discouraged and cannot prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The wicked sharpen axes and seize the imperial throne, attacking people and spreading their poison — yet when a single righteous man is killed, the hearts of the four quarters turn cold, and treacherous ministers and wicked sons grow doubtful and dispirited, unable to have their way.

sentences.zh: 何哉？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 欲所以為彼者，而為我也。

translations.literal: What they intend to do for the sake of others, they actually do for me.
translations.idiomatic: What they mean to accomplish against others, they accomplish for my benefit instead.

sentences.zh: 義在與在，義亡與亡，故王者常推而褒之，所以砥礪生民而窒不軌也。

translations.literal: When righteousness lives I live, when righteousness dies I die — therefore rulers constantly extol and reward it, thus honing the people and choking off the lawless.
translations.idiomatic: Where righteousness stands, I stand; where it falls, I fall — therefore rulers constantly praise and reward such loyalty, to sharpen the moral fiber of the people and cut off the way of the lawless.

sentences.zh: 雖然，非烈丈夫，曷克為之？

translations.literal: Even so, unless one is a stalwart hero, how can one accomplish it?
translations.idiomatic: Still, unless one is a man of resolute courage, how could one achieve such deeds?

sentences.zh: 彼委靡軟熟，偷生自私者，真畏人也哉！

translations.literal: Those who are languid, soft, and complacent, clinging to life out of selfishness — how truly they are to be feared!
translations.idiomatic: Those who are weak and self-serving, clinging to life for selfish ends — how truly they ought to be despised!

sentences.zh: 故次敘夏侯端以來凡三十三人於左方。

translations.literal: Therefore below I record in order, beginning with Xiahou Duan, thirty-three men in all on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, I chronicle below, beginning with Xiahou Duan, thirty-three men in all.

sentences.zh: 夏侯端，壽州壽春人，梁尚書左僕射詳孫也。

translations.literal: Xiahou Duan, a native of Shouchun in Shouzhou, was the grandson of Xiang, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Duan was a native of Shouchun in Shou Prefecture and the grandson of Xiang, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing under the Liang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為大理司直。

translations.literal: He served Sui as a Directing Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as Directing Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 高祖微時與相友，大業中討賊河東，表端為副。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was still obscure he befriended him; during the Daye reign he campaigned against bandits in Hedong and recommended Duan as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: He befriended Gaozu when the latter was still obscure; during the Daye era, when Gaozu campaigned against bandits in Hedong, he recommended Duan as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 端邃數術，密語高祖曰：「玉床搖，帝坐不安。

translations.literal: Duan was skilled in numerology and the arts of prognostication and spoke secretly to Gaozu, saying: "The jade couch sways; the imperial seat is unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Duan was versed in numerology and prognostication and secretly told Gaozu: "The imperial seat trembles and the throne is unsettled.

sentences.zh: 晉得歲，真人將興，安天下之亂者，其在公乎！

translations.literal: Jupiter is in its place of the year; the True Man will rise — he who will still the chaos of the realm, is it not you!
translations.idiomatic: The stars align for the year; a true sovereign will arise — the one who will bring peace to the realm's chaos is surely you!

sentences.zh: 但上性沈忌，內惡諸李，今金才已誅，次且取公，宜蚤為計。」

translations.literal: But the emperor's nature is suspicious and deep, inwardly hating all the Lis; now that Jin Cai has been executed, next he will surely take you — you should plan early."
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor is deep and suspicious, and inwardly hates the Li clan; now that Jin Cai has been executed, you will be next — you should plan ahead."

sentences.zh: 帝感其言。

translations.literal: Gaozu was moved by his words.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was deeply moved by what he said.

sentences.zh: 義師興，端在河東，吏捕送長安。

translations.literal: When the Righteous Army rose, Duan was in Hedong; officials arrested him and sent him to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose in rebellion, Duan was in Hedong; officials arrested him and sent him to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 帝入京師，釋囚，引入臥內，擢秘書監。

translations.literal: When the Emperor entered the capital, he released the prisoners, brought him into his private chamber, and promoted him to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor entered the capital, he released the prisoners, brought Duan into his bedchamber, and appointed him Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 李密之降，關東地未有所屬，端請假節招諭，乃拜大將軍，為河南道招尉使。

translations.literal: After Li Mi surrendered, the lands east of the Pass had no master; Duan requested temporary credentials to summon and persuade, and was appointed Grand General and Commissioner for Summoning and Pacification of Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Mi's surrender, the lands east of the Pass had no clear allegiance; Duan requested imperial credentials to rally the region and was appointed Grand General and Commissioner for Summoning and Pacification of Henan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 即傳檄州縣，東薄海，南揵淮，二十餘州遣使順附。

translations.literal: Immediately he issued proclamations to prefectures and counties; east to the sea, south to the Huai — more than twenty prefectures sent envoys to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately issued proclamations to prefectures and counties; from the coast in the east to the Huai River in the south, more than twenty prefectures sent envoys to submit.

sentences.zh: 次譙州，會亳、汴二州刺史已降王世充，道塞，無所歸，計窮仿徨。

translations.literal: Next at Qiao Prefecture, he found that the prefects of Bo and Bian had already surrendered to Wang Shichong; the road was blocked, nowhere to return, plans exhausted, wandering in distress.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Qiao Prefecture, he found that the prefects of Bo and Bian had already surrendered to Wang Shichong; the road was blocked and he had nowhere to go, and in desperation he wandered aimlessly.

sentences.zh: 麾下二千人糧盡不忍委端去，端乃殺馬宴大澤中，謂眾曰：「我奉王命，義無屈。

translations.literal: Two thousand men under his command, provisions exhausted, could not bear to abandon Duan; Duan then killed horses for a feast in a great marsh and said to the crowd: "I bear the king's command — by righteousness I cannot submit.
translations.idiomatic: His two thousand troops, though their provisions were exhausted, could not bear to leave him; Duan then slaughtered horses for a feast in a great marsh and told the men: "I bear the emperor's command and by duty cannot submit.

sentences.zh: 公等有妻子，徒死無益。

translations.literal: You gentlemen have wives and children; to die in vain is of no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: You have wives and children — to die pointlessly would serve no purpose.

sentences.zh: 吾丐若首，持與賊以取富貴。」

translations.literal: I beg your heads — take them to the bandits to obtain wealth and honor."
translations.idiomatic: Give me your heads — take them to the enemy in exchange for wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 眾號泣不忍視，端亦泣，欲自刎，爭持之，乃止。

translations.literal: The crowd wailed and could not bear to look; Duan wept too, tried to slit his own throat, they struggled to stop him, and so he ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The men wept and could not bear to watch; Duan wept as well, tried to kill himself, and they restrained him until he stopped.

sentences.zh: 行五日，餓死十四三。

translations.literal: After marching five days, four or five out of ten starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: After five days on the march, forty or fifty percent of them had starved to death.

sentences.zh: 遇賊，眾潰，從者才三十餘人，遂東走，擷豆以食。

translations.literal: They encountered bandits; the crowd dispersed; followers numbered barely thirty-plus; they then fled east, gathering beans for food.
translations.idiomatic: They encountered enemy forces and the group scattered; only a little over thirty men remained, and they fled east, gathering wild beans to eat.

sentences.zh: 端持節臥起，嘆曰：「平生不知死地乃在此！」

translations.literal: Duan kept the imperial tally from rising to sleeping and sighed: "All my life I did not know the place of death would be here!"
translations.idiomatic: Duan kept the imperial tally with him at all times and sighed: "I never thought in all my life that I would meet my death in such a place!"

sentences.zh: 縱其下令去，毋俱沒。

translations.literal: He released his subordinates and ordered them to leave — do not all perish together.
translations.idiomatic: He released his subordinates and told them to leave, so they would not all die together.

sentences.zh: 會李公逸守杞州，勒兵迎端。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Gongyi was defending Qi Prefecture; he led troops to welcome Duan.
translations.idiomatic: By chance Li Gongyi was defending Qi Prefecture and led his troops out to welcome Duan.

sentences.zh: 時河南地悉入世充，公逸感端之節，亦固守。

translations.literal: At the time all Henan had entered Wang Shichong's control; Gongyi, moved by Duan's integrity, also held firm.
translations.idiomatic: At that time all of Henan had fallen to Wang Shichong; moved by Duan's steadfastness, Gongyi also held his ground.

sentences.zh: 世充遣人以淮南郡公、尚書少吏部印綬召端，解所服衣以贈。

translations.literal: Shichong sent men with the seals and cords of Duke of Huainan and Vice Director of the Left Selection Bureau of the Masters of Writing to summon Duan, and removed his own garment to give as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong sent envoys bearing the seals and cords of Duke of Huainan and Vice Director of the Left Selection Bureau to summon Duan, and even offered his own robe as a gift.

sentences.zh: 端曰：「吾，天子使，寧汙賊官邪！

translations.literal: Duan said: "I am the emperor's envoy — would I defile myself with a rebel's office!
translations.idiomatic: Duan said: "I am the emperor's envoy — would I stain myself with a traitor's rank!

sentences.zh: 非持首去不可見。」

translations.literal: Unless I carry my head away, I cannot go to see him."
translations.idiomatic: Only by carrying my head away can I go before him."

sentences.zh: 即焚書及衣，因解節毛懷之，間道走宜陽，歷崖峭榛莽。

translations.literal: He immediately burned the letter and garment, then removed the tally tassel and kept it against his chest, took hidden paths toward Yiyang, passing cliffs, precipices, and thorny thickets.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately burned the letter and robe, tucked the tassel of his tally inside his robe, and fled by hidden paths toward Yiyang through steep cliffs and thorny wilderness.

sentences.zh: 比到，其下僅有在者，皆體發臒焦，人不堪視。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, of those who still remained barely any survived; all were gaunt, hair fallen out, skin charred — people could not bear to look.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, of those who had accompanied him almost none remained alive; they were emaciated, their hair fallen out and their skin scorched — unbearable to behold.

sentences.zh: 端入謁，自謝無功，不及危困狀。

translations.literal: Duan entered to pay respects, apologized for having no achievement, and did not mention his peril and hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Duan entered to pay his respects, apologized for his lack of success, and said nothing of the hardships he had endured.

sentences.zh: 帝閔之，復拜秘書監。

translations.literal: The Emperor pitied him and again appointed him Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took pity on him and reappointed him Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出為梓州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Prefect of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Prefect of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 散祿稟周孤窮，不為子孫計。

translations.literal: He distributed his salary to relieve orphans and the poor and did not plan for his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: He gave away his salary to support orphans and the destitute and made no provision for his descendants.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 劉感，岐州鳳泉人，後魏司徒豐生孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Gan, a native of Fengquan in Qizhou, was the grandson of Fengsheng, Grand Minister of State of Northern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gan was a native of Fengquan in Qi Prefecture and the grandson of Fengsheng, Grand Minister of State of Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 武德初，以驃騎將軍戍涇州，為薛仁杲所圍，糧盡，殺所乘馬啖士，而煮骨自飲，至和木屑以食。

translations.literal: Early in Wude, as General of Agile Cavalry he garrisoned Jing Prefecture; besieged by Xue Rengao, provisions exhausted, he killed his mount to feed the soldiers, boiled bones for himself to drink, and even mixed wood shavings into food.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era, as General of Agile Cavalry he garrisoned Jing Prefecture; when besieged by Xue Rengao and their provisions ran out, he slaughtered his horse to feed his men, boiled bones for broth for himself, and even mixed wood shavings into the food.

sentences.zh: 城垂陷，長平王叔良救之，賊乃解。

translations.literal: The city was on the verge of falling; Prince of Changping Shuliang rescued it, and the bandits then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the city was about to fall, Prince of Changping Shuliang came to the rescue and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 與叔良出戰，為賊執，還圍涇州，令感約城中降。

translations.literal: He went out to battle with Shuliang, was captured by the bandits, and when they returned to besiege Jing Prefecture, they had Gan persuade the city to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When he went out to fight alongside Shuliang, he was captured; the rebels brought him back to besiege Jing Prefecture and ordered him to persuade the city to surrender.

sentences.zh: 感紿諾，至城下大呼曰：「賊大饑，亡在朝暮，秦王數十萬眾且至，勉之無苦。」

translations.literal: Gan falsely agreed; reaching below the wall he shouted loudly: "The bandits are greatly famished — destruction is imminent; the Prince of Qin with hundreds of thousands of troops is about to arrive — take heart, do not suffer!"
translations.idiomatic: Gan pretended to agree; when he reached the foot of the wall he shouted: "The rebels are starving and will perish at any moment! The Prince of Qin is coming with an army of hundreds of thousands — hold on, do not lose heart!"

sentences.zh: 仁杲怒，執感埋其半土中，馳射之。

translations.literal: Rengao in anger had Gan seized, buried halfway in earth, and galloped shooting at him.
translations.idiomatic: Rengao flew into a rage, had Gan seized, buried him halfway in the ground, and galloped past shooting at him.

sentences.zh: 至死，詈益甚。

translations.literal: Until death, his curses grew ever fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Until he died, his curses only grew louder.

sentences.zh: 賊平，高祖購得其屍，祭以少牢，贈瀛州刺史，爵平原郡公，封戶二千，謚忠壯。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, Gaozu paid a reward for his corpse, sacrificed to it with a minor offering, posthumously made him Prefect of Yingzhou, enfeoffed him as Duke of Pingyuan with two thousand households, posthumous title Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were defeated, Gaozu offered a reward for his body and performed the minor sacrificial rites; Gan was posthumously appointed Prefect of Ying Prefecture, enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan with two thousand households, and given the posthumous name Loyal and Stalwart.

sentences.zh: 詔其子嗣封爵，賜田宅焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his son to inherit the enfeoffment and granted fields and residence.
translations.idiomatic: An edict permitted his son to inherit the title and granted him land and a residence.

sentences.zh: 常達，陜州陜人。

translations.literal: Chang Da, a native of Shan in Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Da was a native of Shan in Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為鷹擊郎將。

translations.literal: He served Sui as Colonel of Hawk Strikes.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as Colonel of Hawk Strikes.

sentences.zh: 嘗從高祖征伐，與宋老生戰霍邑，軍敗自匿，帝意已死，久乃自歸。

translations.literal: He once followed Gaozu on campaign; at Huoyi he fought Song Laosheng; the army was defeated and he hid himself; the Emperor thought him dead; after a long time he returned of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: He once followed Gaozu on campaign and fought Song Laosheng at Huoyi; when the army was defeated he went into hiding, and the Emperor thought him dead until he finally returned on his own.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，命為統軍，拜隴州刺史。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased, appointed him Army Commander, and made him Prefect of Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was overjoyed, appointed him army commander, and made him Prefect of Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時薛舉方強，達敗其子仁杲，斬首千級。

translations.literal: At the time Xue Ju was powerful; Da defeated his son Rengao and beheaded a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xue Ju was at the height of his power; Da defeated his son Rengao and took a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 舉遣將仵士政紿降，達不疑，厚加撫接。

translations.literal: Ju sent the general Wu Shizheng with a false surrender; Da did not doubt and treated him warmly.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju sent his general Wu Shizheng to feign surrender; Da believed him and treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 士政伺隙劫之，並其眾二千歸賊。

translations.literal: Shizheng watched for an opening and seized him, taking along his two thousand troops back to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Shizheng waited for an opening, captured him, and took his two thousand troops back to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 舉指其妻謂達曰：「識皇后乎？」

translations.literal: Ju pointed to his wife and said to Da: "Do you recognize the Empress?"
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju pointed to his wife and asked Da: "Do you recognize the Empress?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「彼癭老嫗，何所道？」

translations.literal: He answered: "That goitered old crone — what is there to say?"
translations.idiomatic: Da replied: "That old woman with the goiter — what's there to discuss?"

sentences.zh: 舉奴張貴又曰：「亦識我否？」

translations.literal: Ju's slave Zhang Gui also said: "Do you recognize me too?"
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju's slave Zhang Gui then asked: "Do you recognize me as well?"

sentences.zh: 達瞋目曰：「若乃奴耳。」

translations.literal: Da glared and said: "You are merely a slave."
translations.idiomatic: Da glared and said: "You're nothing but a slave."

sentences.zh: 貴忿，舉笏擊其面，達不為懾，亦拔刀逐之，趙弘安為蔽捍，乃免。

translations.literal: Gui in anger raised his tablet and struck his face; Da was not intimidated and also drew a knife to chase him; Zhao Hong'an shielded and protected him, and so he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui in anger raised his tablet and struck Da's face; Da was unafraid and drew his knife to pursue him; Zhao Hong'an shielded him and thus he escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 仁杲平，帝見達，勞曰：「君忠節，正可求之古人。」

translations.literal: When Rengao was pacified, the Emperor saw Da and commended him: "Your loyalty and integrity — one may truly seek such among the ancients."
translations.idiomatic: After Rengao was defeated, the Emperor received Da and praised him: "Your loyalty and steadfastness are qualities one could seek among the ancients."

sentences.zh: 為執士政殺之，賜達布帛三百段，以達並劉感事授史臣令狐德棻雲。

translations.literal: He had Shizheng seized and killed, granted Da three hundred bolts of silk, and entrusted the affairs of Da and Liu Gan together to the historian Linghu Defen.
translations.idiomatic: He had Shizheng seized and executed, granted Da three hundred bolts of silk, and entrusted the stories of Da and Liu Gan to the historian Linghu Defen.

sentences.zh: 終隴西刺史。

translations.literal: He ended as Prefect of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Prefect of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 敬君弘，絳州絳人，北齊尚書右僕射顯俊曾孫也。

translations.literal: Jing Junhong, a native of Jiang in Jiangzhou, was the great-grandson of Xianjun, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing under Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Junhong was a native of Jiang in Jiang Prefecture and the great-grandson of Xianjun, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing under Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 累功歷驃騎將軍，封黔昌侯。

translations.literal: Accumulating merit he rose to General of Agile Cavalry and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Through accumulated merit he rose to General of Agile Cavalry and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qianchang.

sentences.zh: 以屯營兵守玄武門。

translations.literal: With garrison troops he guarded the Xuanwu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the garrison troops guarding the Xuanwu Gate.

sentences.zh: 隱太子之死，左右解散。

translations.literal: At the death of the Hidden Crown Prince, those at his side dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hidden Crown Prince was killed, his attendants scattered.

sentences.zh: 其車騎將軍馮立者，有材武，嘆曰：「生賴其寵，死不共難，我無以見士大夫！」

translations.literal: Among them was Chariot and Cavalry General Feng Li, skilled and martial, who sighed: "In life I relied on his favor; in death I did not share his hardship — I have no face to show gentlemen!"
translations.idiomatic: Among them was Chariot and Cavalry General Feng Li, a capable warrior, who sighed: "In life I enjoyed his favor, yet in death I did not share his peril — how can I face other gentlemen!"

sentences.zh: 乃與巢王親將謝叔方率兵攻玄武門，殊死鬥。

translations.literal: He then with Prince of Qiao's intimate general Xie Shufang led troops to attack the Xuanwu Gate and fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Prince of Qi's close general Xie Shufang in leading troops to attack the Xuanwu Gate, fighting desperately.

sentences.zh: 君弘挺身出，或曰：「事未可判，當按兵待變，成列而鬥可也。」

translations.literal: Junhong stepped forward; someone said: "The matter is not yet decided — you should hold the troops and wait for developments; forming ranks to fight would be better."
translations.idiomatic: Junhong stepped forward boldly; someone advised: "The outcome is not yet clear — you should hold your troops and wait; it would be better to fight in formation."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: He did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 與中郎將呂世衡呼而進，皆戰歿。

translations.literal: With Gentlemen-of-the-House Lü Shiheng he shouted and advanced; both died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He charged forward with Gentlemen-of-the-House Lü Shiheng; both fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 立顧其下曰：「足以報太子矣。」

translations.literal: Li looked back at his subordinates and said: "This is enough to repay the Crown Prince."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Li turned to his men and said: "This is enough to repay the Crown Prince."

sentences.zh: 遂解兵走。

translations.literal: He then disbanded his troops and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He then dismissed his troops and fled.

sentences.zh: 君弘等敗，秦府兵不振。

translations.literal: Junhong and the others were defeated; the Prince of Qin's troops could not rally.
translations.idiomatic: With Junhong defeated, the Prince of Qin's forces were demoralized.

sentences.zh: 尉遲敬德擲巢王首示叔方，叔方下馬慟，亦出奔。

translations.literal: Yuchi Jingde threw Prince of Qiao's head before Shufang; Shufang dismounted in grief and also fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jingde threw the head of the Prince of Qi before Shufang; Shufang dismounted in anguish and fled as well.

sentences.zh: 明日自歸，太宗曰：「義士也。」

translations.literal: The next day he returned of his own accord; Taizong said: "A righteous man."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he surrendered himself; Taizong said: "He is a man of integrity."

sentences.zh: 置之。

translations.literal: He let it pass.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong let the matter rest.

sentences.zh: 俄而立又至，帝讓曰：「汝離我兄弟，罪一也；

translations.literal: Soon Li came again; the Emperor reproached him: "You turned against my brothers — that is the first offense;
translations.idiomatic: Before long Feng Li appeared again; the Emperor rebuked him: "You turned against my brothers — that is your first offense;

sentences.zh: 殺我將士，罪二也。

translations.literal: You killed my officers and soldiers — that is the second offense.
translations.idiomatic: You killed my officers and soldiers — that is your second offense.

sentences.zh: 何所逃死？」

translations.literal: How will you escape death?"
translations.idiomatic: How can you hope to escape death?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「出身事主，當戰之日，不知其它。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Having left home to serve my lord, on the day of battle I knew nothing else."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Having devoted myself to my lord, on the day of battle I thought of nothing else."

sentences.zh: 因伏地悲不自勝，帝亦勞遣之。

translations.literal: He then prostrated himself, grief beyond control; the Emperor also comforted and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated himself, overcome with grief; the Emperor consoled him and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 詔贈君弘左屯衛大將軍，世衡右驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made Junhong Grand General of the Left Rear Guard and Shiheng General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously appointed Junhong Grand General of the Left Rear Guard and Shiheng General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 立已蒙貸，歸語人曰：「上赦吾罪，吾當以死報。」

translations.literal: Li had already been pardoned; returning he told people: "The Emperor has forgiven my crime — I shall repay with my death."
translations.idiomatic: Having been pardoned, Feng Li returned and told others: "The Emperor has forgiven my crime — I shall repay him with my life."

sentences.zh: 未幾，突厥犯便橋，立引數百騎與虜薄，敗之咸陽。

translations.literal: Before long the Turks invaded at Bian Bridge; Li led several hundred horsemen to close with the barbarians and defeated them at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Turks raided at Bian Bridge; Feng Li led several hundred cavalry to engage the enemy and defeated them at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，授廣州都督。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and appointed him Regional Commander of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was delighted and appointed him Regional Commander of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 前日牧守苛肆，為蠻夷患，故數叛。

translations.literal: Previously the prefects and governors were harsh and reckless, becoming a calamity to the barbarian tribes, hence they rebelled repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the local officials had been harsh and tyrannical, oppressing the tribal peoples and causing repeated rebellions.

sentences.zh: 立至，不事家產，衣食弗求贏。

translations.literal: When Li arrived, he did not pursue family wealth; in food and clothing he sought no surplus.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Li arrived, he did not amass property for his family and sought no profit in food or clothing.

sentences.zh: 嘗見貪泉曰：「此豈隱之所酌邪？

translations.literal: Once seeing the Avarice Spring he said: "Is this what the hidden one would drink from?
translations.idiomatic: When he came upon the Avarice Spring he said: "Is this what a man of integrity would drink from?

sentences.zh: 吾雖日汲，庸易吾性哉？」

translations.literal: Though I draw from it daily, would it easily change my nature?"
translations.idiomatic: Even if I draw from it every day, would that easily change my character?"

sentences.zh: 遂極飲去。

translations.literal: He then drank his fill and left.
translations.idiomatic: He then drank his fill and went on.

sentences.zh: 在職不三年，有惠愛，卒於官。

translations.literal: In office less than three years, with kindly benevolence, he died in his post.
translations.idiomatic: He served less than three years, won the people's affection, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 叔方歷伊州刺史，善治軍，戎、華愛之。

translations.literal: Shufang served as Prefect of Yizhou, skilled at governing troops; both barbarians and Chinese loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Shufang served as Prefect of Yi Prefecture and was skilled at military administration; both tribal peoples and Chinese held him in affection.

sentences.zh: 累加銀青光祿大夫，徙洪、廣二州都督。

translations.literal: Cumulative promotion to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal, transferred as Regional Commander of Hong and Guang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and transferred to serve as Regional Commander of Hong and Guang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 卒，謚曰勤。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Diligent.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Diligent.

sentences.zh: 本萬年人，從巢王征討有功，王表為屈咥真府左軍騎雲。

translations.literal: Originally a native of Wannian; following Prince of Qiao on campaigns with merit, the Prince recommended him as Left Army Cavalry Commander of the Quzhan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Originally from Wannian, he followed the Prince of Qi on campaigns with distinction and was recommended by the prince as Left Army Cavalry Commander.

sentences.zh: 呂子臧，蒲州河東人。

translations.literal: Lü Zizang, a native of Hedong in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zizang was a native of Hedong in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 剛直，健於吏。

translations.literal: Upright and firm, capable as an official.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and resolute and excelled in administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末國南陽郡丞，捕擊盜賊有功。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui Daye he was National Assistant Prefect of Nanyang, capturing bandits with merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era he served as Assistant Prefect of Nanyang and distinguished himself in capturing bandits.

sentences.zh: 高祖入京師，遣馬元規慰輯山南，獨子臧堅守。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered the capital, he sent Ma Yuangui to comfort and pacify south of the mountains; Zizang alone held firm.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered the capital, he sent Ma Yuangui to pacify the region south of the mountains, but Zizang alone held his ground.

sentences.zh: 元規遣士諷曉，子臧殺之。

translations.literal: Yuangui sent a soldier to persuade and enlighten him; Zizang killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui sent a messenger to persuade him to surrender; Zizang had the man killed.

sentences.zh: 及煬帝已弒，帝更使其婿薛君倩賫詔，言隋所以亡，諭子臧。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang had been assassinated, the Emperor further sent his son-in-law Xue Junqian bearing an edict, explaining why Sui perished, to instruct Zizang.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yang was assassinated, Gaozu sent his son-in-law Xue Junqian with an edict explaining the fall of the Sui, seeking to persuade Zizang.

sentences.zh: 子臧為故君發喪訖，即送款，就拜鄧州刺史，封南陽郡公。

translations.literal: Zizang held mourning for the former sovereign and then submitted; he was immediately made Prefect of Dengzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zizang held funeral rites for the former emperor and then submitted; he was immediately appointed Prefect of Deng Prefecture and enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 武德初，朱粲新衄，子臧率兵與元規並力。

translations.literal: Early in Wude, Zhu Can had just suffered defeat; Zizang led troops to join forces with Yuangui.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era, after Zhu Can had suffered a fresh defeat, Zizang led troops to join forces with Yuangui.

sentences.zh: 元規軍不進，子臧曰：「乘賊新敗，上下惶沮，一戰可禽；

translations.literal: Yuangui's army would not advance; Zizang said: "While the bandits are freshly defeated, high and low in panic and dejection — one battle can capture them;
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui's army refused to advance; Zizang said: "The enemy has just been defeated and is demoralized — one decisive battle could capture them;

sentences.zh: 若遷延，其眾稍集，吾食盡，致死於我，不可當也。」

translations.literal: If we delay, their followers gradually gather; our food is exhausted — they will fight to the death against us and cannot be withstood."
translations.idiomatic: if we delay, their forces will regroup; once our provisions run out, they will fight us to the death and we cannot hold them off."

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: He did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 子臧請以所部兵獨進，又不許。

translations.literal: Zizang requested to advance alone with his own troops; again not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zizang asked to advance alone with his own troops; again he was refused.

sentences.zh: 俄而粲得眾，復張，元規嬰城，子臧扼腕曰：「謀不見用，坐公死矣。」

translations.literal: Before long Can gathered followers and revived; Yuangui held the city; Zizang wrung his wrists and said: "My plan is not adopted — sitting here we will die."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhu Can regrouped and recovered his strength; Yuangui shut himself in the city; Zizang wrung his hands and said: "Since my advice goes unheeded, we will sit here and die."

sentences.zh: 賊圍固。

translations.literal: The bandits besieged firmly.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels tightened their siege.

sentences.zh: 會霖雨，雉堞崩剝，或勸其降，子臧曰：「我，天子方伯，且降賊乎？」

translations.literal: Rain fell in torrents; the battlements crumbled and peeled; some urged surrender; Zizang said: "I am the emperor's regional governor — would I surrender to bandits?"
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains fell and the walls crumbled; some urged him to surrender; Zizang said: "I am the emperor's regional governor — would I surrender to rebels?"

sentences.zh: 乃率麾下數百人赴敵死，城亦陷，元規死之。

translations.literal: He then led several hundred men under his command to rush the enemy and die; the city also fell; Yuangui died in it.
translations.idiomatic: He then led several hundred of his men to charge the enemy and die fighting; the city fell as well, and Yuangui died with it.

sentences.zh: 元規，安陸人。

translations.literal: Yuangui, a native of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui was a native of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 初以隊正從帝征伐，持節下南陽，得兵萬餘，然無謀，至於敗。

translations.literal: Initially as squad leader he followed the Emperor on campaign, bearing credentials south to Nanyang, obtaining ten thousand-plus troops — yet without strategy, leading to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He had first followed the Emperor on campaign as a squad leader, leading imperial credentials south to Nanyang and raising over ten thousand troops, but he lacked strategic ability and ultimately suffered defeat.

sentences.zh: 王行敏，并州樂平人。

translations.literal: Wang Xingmin, a native of Leping in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingmin was a native of Leping in Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋末為盜長，高祖興，來降，拜潞州刺史，遷屯衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui he was a bandit chief; when Gaozu rose, he came to surrender, was made Prefect of Luzhou, transferred to General of the Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui he was a bandit chief; when Gaozu rose in rebellion he surrendered and was appointed Prefect of Lu Prefecture, then transferred to General of the Garrison Guard.

sentences.zh: 劉武周入并州，寇上黨，取長子、壺關。

translations.literal: Liu Wuzhou entered Bingzhou, raided Shangdang, took Changzi and Huguan.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wuzhou entered Bing Prefecture, he raided Shangdang and captured Changzi and Huguan.

sentences.zh: 或言刺史郭子武懦不支，且失潞，帝遣行敏馳往。

translations.literal: Some said Prefect Guo Ziwu was cowardly and could not hold out, and that Lu would be lost; the Emperor sent Xingmin posthaste.
translations.idiomatic: Reports reached the Emperor that Prefect Guo Ziwu was too timid to hold out and that Lu Prefecture would be lost; the Emperor sent Xingmin there at once.

sentences.zh: 既至，與子武不葉，賊圍急，儲偫空乏，眾恫懼，行敏患之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he did not get along with Ziwu; the bandit siege was urgent; stored provisions empty; the crowd terrified; Xingmin was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, he and Ziwu could not cooperate; the siege was pressing, provisions were exhausted, and the troops were terrified; Xingmin was deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 會有告子武謀反，遂斬之。

translations.literal: It happened that someone reported Ziwu plotting rebellion; he was then beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported that Ziwu was plotting rebellion, Xingmin had him executed.

sentences.zh: 州民陳正謙者，以信義稱鄉里，出粟千石濟軍，由是人自奮，賊乃去。

translations.literal: A local man named Chen Zhengqian, known for faith and righteousness in the district, contributed a thousand shi of grain to aid the army; thereby each man roused himself, and the bandits then departed.
translations.idiomatic: A local man named Chen Zhengqian, renowned in the community for his integrity, contributed a thousand shi of grain to supply the army; inspired by this, the men rallied and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 行敏又敗竇建德兵於武陟。

translations.literal: Xingmin also defeated Dou Jiande's troops at Wuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmin also defeated Dou Jiande's forces at Wuzhi.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，督兵徇燕、趙，與劉黑闥戰歷亭，破之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, supervising troops he subdued Yan and Zhao, fought Liu Heita at Liting, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wude, he led troops through Yan and Zhao, fought Liu Heita at Liting, and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 既而釋甲不設備，為黑闥所掩，縛致麾下。

translations.literal: Soon after he removed armor and set no guard; Heita ambushed him and bound him, bringing him to his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he laid aside his armor and took no precautions; Heita ambushed him, bound him, and brought him to his camp.

sentences.zh: 終不屈，賊遂斬之。

translations.literal: He never yielded; the bandits then beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He never yielded, and the rebels beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 且死，西向跪曰：「臣之忠，惟陛下知之。」

translations.literal: At the point of death, kneeling westward he said: "My loyalty — only Your Majesty knows it."
translations.idiomatic: Facing death, he knelt toward the west and said: "Your Majesty alone knows my loyalty."

sentences.zh: 帝聞而悼惜。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and mourned with regret.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard this, he grieved deeply.

sentences.zh: 黑闥之亂，死事者又有盧士叡、李玄通。

translations.literal: In Heita's rebellion, those who died in service also included Lu Shirui and Li Xuantong.
translations.idiomatic: During Liu Heita's rebellion, Lu Shirui and Li Xuantong also died in the line of duty.

sentences.zh: 士叡客韓城。

translations.literal: Shirui was a guest at Hancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shirui was a resident of Hancheng.

sentences.zh: 隋亂，結納英豪。

translations.literal: When Sui fell into chaos, he gathered and recruited heroes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui dynasty fell into chaos, he gathered and recruited men of ability.

sentences.zh: 高祖與之舊，及兵興，率數百人上謁汾陰，又使兄子諭降劇賊孫華，與劉弘基敗隋將桑顯和於飲馬泉。

translations.literal: Gaozu was old friends with him; when the army rose, he led several hundred men to pay respects at Fenyin; also sent his elder brother's son to persuade the fierce bandit Sun Hua to surrender; with Liu Hongji defeated Sui general Sang Xianhe at Yinma Spring.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had known him for years; when the rebellion began, he led several hundred men to pay homage at Fenyin; he also sent his nephew to persuade the formidable bandit Sun Hua to surrender and, with Liu Hongji, defeated the Sui general Sang Xianhe at Yinma Spring.

sentences.zh: 擢累右光祿大夫，為瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Promoted cumulatively to Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, made Prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and appointed Prefect of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 黑闥遣輕騎破其郛，拒戰半日，士見親屬系虜，乃潰。

translations.literal: Heita sent light cavalry to break his outer wall; resisting half a day, the soldiers saw their kin bound as captives and then routed.
translations.idiomatic: Heita sent light cavalry to breach his outer defenses; after half a day of fighting, his troops saw their families taken captive and broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 士叡為賊擒，欲使說下城堡，不從，見殺。

translations.literal: Shirui was captured by bandits; they wanted him to persuade castles to surrender; he refused and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shirui was captured; the rebels wanted him to persuade fortified cities to surrender, but he refused and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 玄通，藍田人。

translations.literal: Xuantong, a native of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuantong was a native of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 為隋鷹揚郎將，高祖入關，率所部自歸，拜定州總管。

translations.literal: He was Sui Colonel of Flying Hawks; when Gaozu entered the Pass, he led his command to surrender of his own accord, appointed General Commandant of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He had served the Sui as Colonel of Flying Hawks; when Gaozu entered the Pass, he led his troops to surrender and was appointed General Commandant of Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為黑闥所破，愛其才，欲以為將。

translations.literal: Defeated by Heita, who admired his talent and wished to make him a general.
translations.idiomatic: After being defeated by Heita, who admired his talent and wished to make him a general.

sentences.zh: 玄通曰：「吾當守節以報，烏能降誌賊邪？」

translations.literal: Xuantong said: "I should uphold integrity to repay — how could I lower my resolve to bandits?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuantong said: "I must uphold my integrity in repayment — how could I lower myself to serve a rebel?"

sentences.zh: 不聽，囚之。

translations.literal: He did not listen and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Heita would not listen and had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 故吏有餉飲饋者，玄通曰：「諸君見哀，吾能一醉。」

translations.literal: Former subordinates brought drink and food; Xuantong said: "You gentlemen pity me — I can get drunk once."
translations.idiomatic: Former subordinates brought him food and drink; Xuantong said: "You pity me — let me have one last drink."

sentences.zh: 遂縱飲，謂守者曰：「吾能劍舞，可借刀。」

translations.literal: He then drank freely and said to the guards: "I can perform a sword dance — lend me a blade."
translations.idiomatic: He drank freely and said to his guards: "I can perform a sword dance — lend me a sword."

sentences.zh: 守士與之。

translations.literal: The guards gave him one.
translations.idiomatic: The guards gave him one.

sentences.zh: 曲終，仰天太息曰：「大丈夫撫方面，不能保所守，尚可視息邪？」

translations.literal: When the song ended, sighing heavenward he said: "A great man governing a region — unable to hold what he guards — can he still draw breath?"
translations.idiomatic: When the dance ended, he sighed toward heaven and said: "A man who governed a region yet could not hold what he was charged to defend — how can he still go on living?"

sentences.zh: 乃潰腹死。

translations.literal: He then disemboweled himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: He then ran himself through and died.

sentences.zh: 帝為流涕，擢其子伏護大將軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor wept for him and promoted his son Fuhu to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wept and promoted his son Fuhu to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 羅士信，齊州歷城人。

translations.literal: Luo Shixin, a native of Licheng in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shixin was a native of Licheng in Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋大業時，長白山賊王薄、左才相、孟讓攻齊郡，通守張須陀率兵擊賊。

translations.literal: During Sui Daye, Changbai Mountain bandits Wang Bo, Zuo Caixiang, and Meng Rang attacked Qi Prefecture; Circuit Defender Zhang Xituo led troops to strike the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era, the Changbai Mountain bandits Wang Bo, Zuo Caixiang, and Meng Rang attacked Qi Prefecture; Circuit Defender Zhang Xituo led troops against them.

sentences.zh: 士信以執衣，年十四，短而悍，請自效。

translations.literal: Shixin served as robe-bearer; age fourteen, short but fierce, he requested to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin served as a personal attendant; at fourteen he was short but fierce and volunteered for service.

sentences.zh: 須陀疑其不勝甲，少之。

translations.literal: Xituo doubted he could bear armor and slighted him.
translations.idiomatic: Xituo doubted he could wear armor and underestimated him.

sentences.zh: 士信怒，被重甲，左右，上馬顧眄。

translations.literal: Shixin in anger donned heavy armor, walked right and left, mounted a horse and looked about.
translations.idiomatic: Angered, Shixin put on heavy armor, strutted back and forth, mounted a horse, and looked about proudly.

sentences.zh: 須陀許之。

translations.literal: Xituo assented.
translations.idiomatic: Xituo agreed to let him fight.

sentences.zh: 擊賊濰水上，陣才列，執長矛馳入賊營，刺殺數人，取一級擲之，承以矛，戴而行，賊皆眙懼無敢亢。

translations.literal: Striking bandits on the Wei River, the formation just deployed — gripping a long spear he galloped into the bandit camp, stabbed and killed several men, took one head and tossed it, caught it on his spear, wore it and walked; all bandits stared in fear, none dared resist.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle on the Wei River, as the lines were forming, he galloped into the rebel camp with a long spear, killed several men, severed a head and impaled it on his spear, and walked along displaying it; the rebels stared in terror and none dared oppose him.

sentences.zh: 須陀乘之，大破賊。

translations.literal: Xituo pressed the advantage and routed the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Xituo pressed the advantage and routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 士信逐北，每殺一賊，輒劓鼻納諸懷，暨還，驗以代級。

translations.literal: Shixin pursued the fleeing; each time he killed a bandit he cut off the nose and put it in his bosom; on return they were counted in place of heads.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin pursued the fleeing enemy; for each rebel he killed he cut off the nose and tucked it in his robe; on return they were counted in place of severed heads.

sentences.zh: 須陀嘆伏，遺以所乘馬。

translations.literal: Xituo sighed in admiration and gave him the horse he rode.
translations.idiomatic: Xituo marveled and gave him his own horse.

sentences.zh: 凡戰，須陀先登，士信副，以為常。

translations.literal: In every battle Xituo mounted first, Shixin second — this became the rule.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle Xituo led the charge and Shixin followed — this became their custom.

sentences.zh: 煬帝遣使圖須陀、士信陣法上內史。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang sent envoys to depict Xituo and Shixin's battle formations and submit them to the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang sent envoys to have the battle formations of Xituo and Shixin recorded and submitted to the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後須陀為李密所殺，士信與裴仁基歸密，署總管，俾統所部討王世充。

translations.literal: Later Xituo was killed by Li Mi; Shixin and Pei Renji joined Mi, appointed Supervisor, tasked to command his own troops against Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xituo was killed by Li Mi; Shixin and Pei Renji joined Li Mi; Shixin was appointed Supervisor and charged with leading his own troops against Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 身被重創，見獲於世充。

translations.literal: His body bearing grave wounds, he was captured by Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Severely wounded, he was captured by Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 世充愛其才，厚遇之，與同寢食。

translations.literal: Shichong admired his talent, treated him generously, ate and slept with him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong admired his ability, treated him generously, and even shared meals and lodging with him.

sentences.zh: 後得密將邴元真等，故士信稍稍疏斥。

translations.literal: Later obtaining Li Mi's generals Bing Yuanzhen and others, Shixin was gradually sidelined and cold-shouldered.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wang Shichong captured Li Mi's generals including Bing Yuanzhen, Shixin was gradually marginalized.

sentences.zh: 士信恥與伍，率所部千餘人來降高祖，拜陜州道行軍總管，因謀世充。

translations.literal: Shixin ashamed to be among them, led over a thousand of his troops to surrender to Gaozu, appointed Grand General on Campaign for Shanzhou Circuit, and plotted against Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed to remain among them, Shixin led more than a thousand of his men to surrender to Gaozu; he was appointed Grand General on Campaign for Shanzhou Circuit and plotted against Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 士信行則先鋒，反則殿，有所獲，悉散戲下有功者，或脫衣解馬賜之，士以故用命。

translations.literal: Shixin in advance was vanguard, in retreat rearguard; whatever was seized he wholly distributed among subordinates with merit, sometimes stripping off garments or giving horses as gifts; soldiers therefore obeyed with full effort.
translations.idiomatic: In advance Shixin served as vanguard; in retreat he covered the rear; he distributed all spoils among deserving subordinates and sometimes gave away his own clothes and horses; his men therefore fought with total devotion.

sentences.zh: 然持法嚴，至親舊無少貸，其下亦不甚附。

translations.literal: Yet he held the law strictly, not sparing even close kin and old friends; his subordinates also did not greatly attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he enforced the law strictly, showing no leniency even to close friends and relatives, and his subordinates were not deeply devoted to him.

sentences.zh: 師次洛陽，攻千金堡，堡有惡言訽軍，士信怒，夜遣百人載嬰兒啼噪堡下，若自東都出奔者，既而陽悟曰：「非也，此千金堡耳。」

translations.literal: The army halted at Luoyang, attacking Qianjin Fort; the fort had harsh words reviling the army; Shixin in anger by night sent a hundred men carrying infants whose crying filled below the fort, as if fleeing from the Eastern Capital; then feigning realization said: "No — this is Qianjin Fort."
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Luoyang and attacked Qianjin Fort, the garrison hurled insults at the troops; Shixin in anger sent a hundred men by night carrying infants whose crying echoed below the fort, as if refugees were fleeing from the Eastern Capital; then they pretended to realize: "No — this is Qianjin Fort."

sentences.zh: 因散去。

translations.literal: They then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: They then dispersed.

sentences.zh: 堡兵開門追掠，士信伏入，屠之無類。

translations.literal: Fort soldiers opened the gate to pursue and plunder; Shixin ambushed and entered, slaughtering to the last.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison opened the gates to pursue and plunder; Shixin's men sprang the ambush and slaughtered every soul inside.

sentences.zh: 賊平，授絳州總管，封郯國公。

translations.literal: When bandits were pacified, granted General Commandant of Jiangzhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Tan.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were defeated, he was appointed General Commandant of Jiang Prefecture and enfeoffed as Duke of Tan.

sentences.zh: 從秦王擊劉黑闥洛水上，得一城，王君廓戍之，賊急攻，潰而出。

translations.literal: Following the Prince of Qin attacking Liu Heita on the Luo River, they took a city; Wang Junguo garrisoned it; bandits pressed the attack urgently; he broke out in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Prince of Qin in attacking Liu Heita on the Luo River, they captured a city and Wang Junguo was assigned to garrison it; the rebels attacked fiercely and Junguo broke out in defeat.

sentences.zh: 王語諸將：「孰能守此？」

translations.literal: The Prince spoke to the generals: "Who can hold this?"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince asked his generals: "Who can hold this city?"

sentences.zh: 士信曰：「願以守。」

translations.literal: Shixin said: "I wish to hold it."
translations.idiomatic: Shixin said: "I will hold it."

sentences.zh: 乃命之。

translations.literal: He then ordered him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince appointed him.

sentences.zh: 士信已入，賊悉眾攻，方雨雪，救軍不得進。

translations.literal: Shixin had entered; bandits attacked with full force; just then rain and snow; relief troops could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shixin was inside, the rebels attacked with their full strength; rain and snow fell, and relief troops could not reach him.

sentences.zh: 城陷，黑闥欲用之，不屈而死，年二十八。

translations.literal: The city fell; Heita wished to employ him; he would not yield and died, age twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell; Heita wished to employ him, but Shixin refused to submit and was killed at the age of twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 王隱悼，購其屍以葬，謚曰勇。

translations.literal: The Prince grieved in secret, paid for his corpse to bury, posthumous title Brave.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince mourned in private, ransomed his body for burial, and gave him the posthumous name Brave.

sentences.zh: 初，士信為仁基所禮，及東都平，出家財斂葬北邙以報德，且曰：「我死當墓其側。」

translations.literal: Initially Shixin was honored by Renji; when the Eastern Capital was pacified, he spent family wealth to gather and bury on Northern Mang to repay kindness, and said: "When I die I shall be buried at his side."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shixin had been treated with honor by Pei Renji; when the Eastern Capital was pacified, he spent his family fortune to have Renji buried on Northern Mang to repay his kindness, saying: "When I die, bury me at his side."

sentences.zh: 至是，如所誌。

translations.literal: At this time, as he had vowed.
translations.idiomatic: When the time came, it was done as he had wished.

sentences.zh: 張道源，并州祁人，名河，以字顯。

translations.literal: Zhang Daoyuan, a native of Qi in Bingzhou; personal name He, style name used for display.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Daoyuan was a native of Qi in Bing Prefecture; his given name was He, but he was known by his style name.

sentences.zh: 年十四，居父喪，士人賢其孝，縣令郭湛署所居曰復禮鄉至孝裏。

translations.literal: Age fourteen, observing father's mourning; gentlemen admired his filial piety; Magistrate Guo Zhan labeled his residence Fuli Village, Village of Utmost Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen, while mourning his father, local scholars praised his filial devotion; Magistrate Guo Zhan named his neighborhood Fuli Village, Lane of Utmost Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 道源嘗與客夜宿，客暴死，道源恐主人忽怖，臥屍側，至署乃告，又徒步護送還其家。

translations.literal: Daoyuan once lodged overnight with a guest who suddenly died; Daoyuan feared the host would be startled and frightened, lay beside the corpse until dawn then reported it, and also walked on foot escorting the body back to his home.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan once lodged overnight with a guest who died suddenly; fearing the innkeeper would be terrified, he slept beside the corpse until morning before informing anyone, then walked the body home on foot.

sentences.zh: 隋末政亂，辭監察御史，歸閭里。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui when government was chaotic, he resigned as Investigating Censor and returned to his village.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui government collapsed into chaos, he resigned as Investigating Censor and returned home.

sentences.zh: 高祖興，署大將軍府戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu rose, appointed Staff Officer of the Household Bureau in the Grand General's Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu rose in rebellion, he was appointed Staff Officer of the Household Bureau in the Grand General's Office.

sentences.zh: 至賈胡堡，復使守并州。

translations.literal: Reaching Jiahu Fort, again sent to guard Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Jiahu Fort, he was again assigned to defend Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 京師平，遣撫慰山東，下燕、趙。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, sent to comfort and pacify Shandong, subduing Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was pacified, he was sent to pacify Shandong and brought Yan and Zhao under control.

sentences.zh: 有詔褒美，封累范陽郡公。

translations.literal: An edict praised and commended him; enfeoffed cumulatively as Duke of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict praised his service and he was enfeoffed as Duke of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 淮安王神通略定山東，令守趙州，為竇建德所執。

translations.literal: Prince of Huai'an Wang Shentong broadly pacified Shandong, ordered him to guard Zhaozhou; captured by Dou Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Huai'an Wang Shentong pacified Shandong, Daoyuan was ordered to hold Zhao Prefecture and was captured by Dou Jiande.

sentences.zh: 會建德寇河南，間遣人詣朝，請乘虛搗賊心脅。

translations.literal: When Jiande raided Henan, secretly sent men to court, requesting to strike the bandits' heartland while they were exposed.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiande raided Henan, Daoyuan secretly sent envoys to court, urging an attack on the enemy's rear while their main force was away.

sentences.zh: 即詔諸將率兵影接。

translations.literal: Immediately an edict ordered generals to lead troops in shadowing support.
translations.idiomatic: An edict immediately ordered the generals to march in support.

sentences.zh: 俄而賊平，還，拜大理卿。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits were pacified; he returned and was appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels were defeated; he returned and was appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時何稠得罪，籍其家屬賜群臣。

translations.literal: At the time He Chou was condemned; his family members were registered and bestowed on the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At that time He Chou had fallen from favor; his family members were confiscated and distributed among the court officials.

sentences.zh: 道源曰：「禍福何常，安可利人之亡，取其子女自奉？

translations.literal: Daoyuan said: "Fortune and misfortune — how constant are they? How can one profit from another's ruin and take his sons and daughters to serve oneself?
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan said: "Fortune and misfortune are unpredictable — how can one profit from another's ruin and take his children for one's own service?

sentences.zh: 仁者不為也。」

translations.literal: The benevolent would not do this."
translations.idiomatic: A man of benevolence would not do such a thing."

sentences.zh: 更資以衣食遣之。

translations.literal: He instead supplied them with food and clothing and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he provided them with food and clothing and sent them on their way.

sentences.zh: 天子見其年耆，拜綿州刺史。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven saw his advanced age and appointed him Prefect of Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his advanced age, the Emperor appointed him Prefect of Mian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書，謚曰節。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Minister of Works; posthumous title Steadfast.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Minister of Works, with the posthumous name Steadfast.

sentences.zh: 道源雖官九卿，無產貲，比亡，余粟二斛。

translations.literal: Though Daoyuan held rank among the Nine Ministers, he had no property; by the time of his death, only two hu of grain remained.
translations.idiomatic: Although Daoyuan held one of the Nine Ministers' posts, he owned no property; at his death only two hu of grain remained.

sentences.zh: 詔賜帛三百段。

translations.literal: An edict granted three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 族孫楚金有至行，與兄越石皆舉進士。

translations.literal: Clansman Chujin had utmost conduct; with elder brother Yueshi both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Chujin was a man of exceptional character; he and his elder brother Yueshi both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 州欲獨薦楚金，固辭，請俱罷。

translations.literal: The prefecture wished to recommend Chujin alone; he firmly declined, requesting both be passed over.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefecture wished to recommend Chujin alone, he firmly declined and asked that both brothers be passed over.

sentences.zh: 都督李勣嘆曰：「士求才行者也。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Li Ji sighed and said: "Scholars are sought for ability and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Li Ji exclaimed: "Scholars are valued for their ability and character.

sentences.zh: 既能讓，何嫌皆取乎？」

translations.literal: Since he can yield, why hesitate to take both?"
translations.idiomatic: If he is capable of yielding, why not recommend them both?"

sentences.zh: 乃並薦之。

translations.literal: He then recommended both.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended both brothers.

sentences.zh: 累進刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Cumulative promotion to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳初，彗見東井，上疏陳得失。

translations.literal: Early in Yifeng, a comet appeared in the Eastern Well; he submitted a memorial stating strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yifeng era, when a comet appeared in the Eastern Well constellation, he submitted a memorial analyzing the state's strengths and weaknesses.

sentences.zh: 高宗欽納，賜物二百段。

translations.literal: Gaozong respectfully accepted it and granted two hundred items.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong accepted it with approval and granted him two hundred gifts.

sentences.zh: 武后時，歷秋官尚書，爵南陽侯。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's time, served as Minister of Punishments, enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he served as Minister of Punishments and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 有清概，然尚文刻，當時亦少之。

translations.literal: He had pure integrity, yet valued literary harshness; at the time few were like him.
translations.idiomatic: He had a reputation for integrity, though he favored strict literary standards; even in his own day he was little understood.

sentences.zh: 為酷吏所構，流死嶺表。

translations.literal: Framed by cruel officials, he was exiled and died beyond the mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: Framed by cruel officials, he was exiled and died in the far south.

sentences.zh: 李育德，趙州人。

translations.literal: Li Yude, a native of Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yude was a native of Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖諤，仕隋通州刺史，為名臣。

translations.literal: Grandfather E served Sui as Prefect of Tongzhou and was a renowned minister.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather E had served the Sui as Prefect of Tong Prefecture and was a renowned official.

sentences.zh: 世富於財，家僮百人。

translations.literal: The family was wealthy in property, with a hundred household servants.
translations.idiomatic: The family was wealthy and kept a hundred household servants.

sentences.zh: 天下亂，乃私完械甲，嬰武陟城自保，人多從之，遂為長。

translations.literal: When the realm fell into chaos, he privately completed armor and weapons, held Wuzhi city to protect himself, many followed him, and he became a leader.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire fell into chaos, he privately gathered arms and armor, fortified Wuzhi city for self-defense, and many joined him until he became their leader.

sentences.zh: 劇賊來掠，不能克。

translations.literal: Fierce bandits came to plunder but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Formidable bandits came to raid but could not defeat him.

sentences.zh: 隋亡，與柳燮等歸李密，私署總管。

translations.literal: When Sui perished, with Liu Xie and others he joined Li Mi and was privately appointed Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: After the Sui fell, he joined Li Mi with Liu Xie and others and was appointed Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 密為王世充所破，以郡來降，即拜陟州刺史。

translations.literal: Mi was defeated by Wang Shichong; he surrendered with the commandery and was immediately made Prefect of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Mi was defeated by Wang Shichong, Yude surrendered with his commandery and was immediately appointed Prefect of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 兄厚德，自賊所逃歸，度河復被執。

translations.literal: Elder brother Houde, escaping from the bandits, crossed the river but was captured again.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Houde escaped from the rebels but was captured again while crossing the river.

sentences.zh: 賊使招育德，陽許之，故兄不死。

translations.literal: The bandits sent to summon Yude; he falsely agreed, and so his brother was not killed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent to summon Yude; he pretended to agree, and thus his brother was spared.

sentences.zh: 賊帥段大師令裨校以兵守厚德，陰得其歡，乃與州人賈慈行謀逐賊。

translations.literal: Bandit chief Duan Dashi ordered lieutenants with troops to guard Houde; secretly winning their favor, he then with local man Jia Cixing plotted to drive out the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Duan Dashi assigned troops to guard Houde; Yude secretly won them over and, with a local man named Jia Cixing, plotted to expel the rebels.

sentences.zh: 慈行夜登城呼曰：「唐兵登矣！」

translations.literal: Cixing by night mounted the wall and shouted: "Tang troops have mounted the wall!"
translations.idiomatic: Cixing climbed the wall at night and shouted: "The Tang army is on the wall!"

sentences.zh: 厚德自獄擁群囚噪而出，斬長史，眾不敢動，大師縋城走。

translations.literal: Houde from prison led a crowd of prisoners clamoring out, beheaded the Chief Administrator, the crowd dared not move, and Dashi lowered himself from the wall and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Houde led the prisoners out of jail in a clamor, beheaded the chief administrator, and when no one dared move, Dashi lowered himself from the wall and fled.

sentences.zh: 即拜殷州刺史。

translations.literal: He was immediately made Prefect of Yinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Houde was immediately appointed Prefect of Yin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 厚德省親，留育德以守，引兵拔賊河內堡三十一所。

translations.literal: Houde visited his family, leaving Yude to hold the post; he led troops and captured thirty-one rebel forts in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: When Houde went home to visit his family, he left Yude to hold the prefecture and led troops to capture thirty-one rebel forts in Henei.

sentences.zh: 世充怒，悉銳士攻之，城陷，猶力戰，與三弟皆歿。

translations.literal: Shichong in anger sent all his elite troops to attack; the city fell; he still fought fiercely; with three younger brothers all perished.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong in fury sent his best troops against him; when the city fell Yude fought on, and he and his three younger brothers all perished.

sentences.zh: 時死節者又有李公逸、張善相，凡三人。

translations.literal: At the time those who died upholding integrity also included Li Gongyi and Zhang Shanxiang — three men in all.
translations.idiomatic: Others who died upholding their integrity at that time included Li Gongyi and Zhang Shanxiang — three men in all.

sentences.zh: 公逸者，與族弟善行居雍丘，以材雄，為眾所歸。

translations.literal: Gongyi, with clansman younger brother Shanxing, lived at Yongqiu; for his heroic talent he was followed by the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi lived at Yongqiu with his clansman Shanxing; his ability and courage won him a large following.

sentences.zh: 始附王世充，策其必敗，乃獻款高祖，因其地置杞州，即拜總管，封陽夏郡公。

translations.literal: Initially he attached to Wang Shichong, calculated that he must fail, then submitted to Gaozu; on account of his territory Qi Prefecture was established; he was immediately made General Commandant and enfeoffed as Duke of Yangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He had initially sided with Wang Shichong but foresaw his defeat and submitted to Gaozu; his territory was made Qi Prefecture, and he was appointed General Commandant and enfeoffed as Duke of Yangxia.

sentences.zh: 以善行為刺史。

translations.literal: Shanxing was made Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxing was appointed prefect.

sentences.zh: 世充遣其弟將徐、亳兵攻之，公逸請援，未報，因使善行守，身入朝言狀。

translations.literal: Shichong sent his younger brother leading Xu and Bo troops to attack; Gongyi requested relief, with no reply; he therefore had Shanxing hold the post while he himself entered court to report the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong sent his brother with troops from Xu and Bo to attack; Gongyi requested reinforcements but received no reply, so he left Shanxing to hold the city and went to court himself to report the situation.

sentences.zh: 至襄城，為賊邏送洛陽。

translations.literal: Reaching Xiangcheng, he was intercepted by bandits and sent to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangcheng he was intercepted by enemy patrols and sent to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 世充曰：「君越鄭臣唐，何哉？」

translations.literal: Shichong said: "You crossed from Zheng to serve Tang — why?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong said: "You abandoned Zheng to serve Tang — why?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「我於天下唯聞有唐。」

translations.literal: He answered: "In the realm I have heard only of Tang."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "In all the realm I have heard only of Tang."

sentences.zh: 賊怒斬之。

translations.literal: The bandits in anger beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in anger had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 善行亦死。

translations.literal: Shanxing also died.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxing died as well.

sentences.zh: 帝悼惜，封其子襄邑縣公。

translations.literal: The Emperor mourned with regret and enfeoffed his son as Duke of Xiangyi County.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grieved and enfeoffed his son as Duke of Xiangyi County.

sentences.zh: 善相，襄城人。

translations.literal: Shanxiang, a native of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shanxiang was a native of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 大業末為里長，督兵跡盜，為眾附賴，乃據許州奉李密。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he was village head, supervising troops to track bandits; trusted by the masses, he then held Xuzhou and served Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era he served as village head, leading troops against bandits; trusted by the people, he seized Xu Prefecture and pledged allegiance to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 密敗，挈州以來，詔即授伊州總管。

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated, he brought the prefecture to surrender; an edict immediately made him General Commandant of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Mi's defeat he brought the prefecture over to Tang and was immediately appointed General Commandant of Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王世充攻之，屢困賊，遣使三輩請救，朝廷未暇也。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong attacked him; he repeatedly distressed the bandits; sent envoys three times requesting relief; the court had no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong attacked him; he repeatedly inflicted losses on the enemy and sent three envoys requesting relief, but the court had no time to respond.

sentences.zh: 會糧盡，眾餓死，善相謂僚屬曰：「吾為唐臣，當效命。

translations.literal: When provisions ran out and the crowd starved to death, Shanxiang said to his staff: "I am a minister of Tang — I should devote my life.
translations.idiomatic: When provisions ran out and his men began starving to death, Shanxiang told his staff: "I am a minister of Tang and must do my duty.

sentences.zh: 君等無庸死，斬吾首以下賊可也。」

translations.literal: You gentlemen need not die — cut off my head and present it below to the bandits and that will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: You need not die — cut off my head and offer it to the enemy and that will suffice."

sentences.zh: 眾泣不肯，曰：「與公同死，愈於獨生。」

translations.literal: The crowd wept and refused, saying: "To die with you, lord, is better than living alone."
translations.idiomatic: They wept and refused, saying: "To die with you is better than living on alone."

sentences.zh: 城陷被執，罵賊見殺。

translations.literal: The city fell; he was seized; cursing the bandits he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he was captured; he cursed the rebels and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘆曰：「吾負善相，善相不負我！」

translations.literal: Gaozu sighed: "I failed Shanxiang — Shanxiang did not fail me!"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sighed: "I failed Shanxiang, but Shanxiang did not fail me!"

sentences.zh: 乃封其子襄城郡公。

translations.literal: He then enfeoffed his son as Duke of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then enfeoffed Shanxiang's son as Duke of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 高叡，京兆萬年人，隋尚書左僕射颎孫也。

translations.literal: Gao Rui, a native of Wannian in Jingzhao, was the grandson of Yong, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing under Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rui was a native of Wannian in the capital region and the grandson of Yong, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 舉明經，稍遷通義令，有治勞，人刻石載德。

translations.literal: Passed the Mingjing examination, gradually promoted to Magistrate of Tongyi; with administrative merit, people carved stone to record his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination and rose to Magistrate of Tongyi; the people carved a stone monument to record his virtue in office.

sentences.zh: 歷趙州刺史，平昌縣子。

translations.literal: Served as Prefect of Zhaozhou, Viscount of Pingchang County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Prefect of Zhao Prefecture and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Pingchang County.

sentences.zh: 聖歷初，突厥默啜入寇，叡嬰城拒，虜攻益急。

translations.literal: Early in Shengli, the Türk Mo-chuo invaded; Rui held the city in defense; the barbarians pressed the attack ever more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shengli era, when the Türk leader Mo-chuo invaded, Rui shut himself in the city to resist, and the enemy attack grew ever fiercer.

sentences.zh: 長史唐波若度且陷，即與虜通。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Tang Boruo judged that it would soon fall and immediately communicated with the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Administrator Tang Boruo saw that the city would soon fall, he secretly contacted the enemy.

sentences.zh: 叡覺之，力不能制，即自經。

translations.literal: Rui detected it but lacked the power to control it; he then hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Rui discovered the treachery but could not stop it and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 不得死，為虜執，使降諭諸縣，不肯應，見殺。

translations.literal: He could not die; captured by the barbarians, they had him persuade the counties to surrender; he refused to respond and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He failed to kill himself and was captured; the enemy ordered him to persuade the surrounding counties to surrender, but he refused and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 初，虜至，有為叡計者：「突厥蜂銳，所向無完，公不能亢，且當下之。」

translations.literal: Initially when the barbarians arrived, someone advised Rui: "The Türks swarm and are sharp; wherever they go nothing remains intact — you cannot resist; you should submit for now."
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy first arrived, someone advised Rui: "The Türks are fierce and unstoppable — you cannot hold them off; you should submit for now."

sentences.zh: 答曰：「我，刺史，不戰而降，罪大矣。」

translations.literal: He answered: "I am the prefect — to surrender without fighting is a great crime."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "I am the prefect — to surrender without a fight would be an unforgivable crime."

sentences.zh: 武后嘆惜，贈冬官尚書，謚曰節。

translations.literal: Empress Wu mourned with regret, posthumously made him Minister of Public Works, posthumous title Steadfast.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu grieved and posthumously appointed him Minister of Public Works, with the posthumous name Steadfast.

sentences.zh: 詔誅波若，籍其家。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Boruo executed and his household registered for confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Boruo executed and his property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 下制暴叡忠節、波若臣賊，使天下知之。

translations.literal: An edict was issued proclaiming Rui's loyalty and steadfastness and Boruo's treachery to the bandits, so the realm would know.
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed Rui's loyalty and Boruo's treachery so that all the realm would know.

sentences.zh: 子仲舒，通故訓學，擢明經，為相王府文學，王所欽器。

translations.literal: His son Zhongshu, versed in the old classics and instruction, passed the Mingjing examination, served as Literary Attendant in the Prince of Xiang's household, and was highly esteemed by the prince.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongshu, versed in the classics, passed the Mingjing examination and served as Literary Attendant in the Prince of Xiang's household, where the prince held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 開元初，宋璟、蘇颋當秉，多咨訪焉。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan, Song Jing and Su Ting held power and frequently consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era, when Song Jing and Su Ting held power, they frequently sought his counsel.

sentences.zh: 時舍人崔琳練達政宜，璟等禮異之。

translations.literal: At the time Attendant Cui Lin was skilled in affairs of government; Jing and the others treated him with special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Attendant Cui Lin was skilled in affairs of state, and Jing and the others treated him with special respect.

sentences.zh: 常語人曰：「古事問高仲舒，時事問崔琳，何復疑？」

translations.literal: He often told people: "For ancient matters ask Gao Zhongshu; for current affairs ask Cui Lin — what further doubt remains?"
translations.idiomatic: He often said: "For ancient matters ask Gao Zhongshu; for current affairs ask Cui Lin — what more is there to doubt?"

sentences.zh: 終太子右庶子。

translations.literal: He ended as Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 安金藏，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: An Jinzang, a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: An Jinzang was a native of Chang'an in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 在太常工籍。

translations.literal: He was on the artisan registry of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was registered as an artisan with the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 睿宗為皇嗣，少府監裴匪躬、中官範雲仙坐私謁皇嗣，皆殊死，自是公卿不復見，唯工優給使得進。
