translations.literal: Ruizong was Heir Apparent; Director of the Palace Manufactories Pei Feigong and palace eunuch Fan Yunxian were condemned to death for privately visiting the Heir Apparent; from then on ministers no longer saw him — only artisans and performers, specially supplied, were permitted entry.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong was Heir Apparent, Director of the Palace Manufactories Pei Feigong and the eunuch Fan Yunxian were executed for visiting him privately; thereafter no court officials were permitted to see him — only artisans and performers were allowed in.

sentences.zh: 俄有誣皇嗣異謀者，武后詔來俊臣問狀，左右畏慘楚，欲引服。

translations.literal: Soon someone falsely accused the Heir Apparent of plotting rebellion; Empress Wu ordered Lai Junchen to investigate; those around him feared torture and wished to confess.
translations.idiomatic: Soon someone falsely accused the Heir Apparent of plotting rebellion; Empress Wu ordered Lai Junchen to investigate; those around Ruizong feared torture and were ready to confess.

sentences.zh: 金藏大呼曰：「公不信我言，請剖心以明皇嗣不反也。」

translations.literal: Jinzang shouted loudly: "If you do not believe my words, I beg to cut open my heart to prove the Heir Apparent has not rebelled."
translations.idiomatic: Jinzang cried out: "If you will not believe me, let me cut open my heart to prove the Heir Apparent has not rebelled."

sentences.zh: 引佩刀自剚腹中，腸出被地，眩而仆。

translations.literal: He drew his belt knife and stabbed his own belly; his intestines spilled onto the ground; dizzy, he collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his belt knife and stabbed himself in the belly; his intestines spilled onto the ground and he collapsed in a faint.

sentences.zh: 後聞大驚，輿致禁中，命高醫內腸，褫桑<者土>紩之，閱夕而蘇。

translations.literal: The Empress heard and was greatly shocked; he was carried into the inner palace; she ordered skilled physicians to replace his intestines, stripped mulberry-hemp cloth to bind them, and by the next evening he revived.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress was shocked; he was carried into the palace, skilled physicians restored his intestines and bound the wound with cloth, and by the next evening he had revived.

sentences.zh: 後臨視，嘆曰：「吾有子不能自明，不如爾之忠也。」

translations.literal: The Empress came to see him and sighed: "I have a son who cannot clear himself — he is not as loyal as you."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress came to see him and sighed: "My own son could not clear himself — he is not as loyal as you."

sentences.zh: 即詔停獄，睿宗乃安。

translations.literal: She immediately ordered the investigation halted, and Ruizong was then secure.
translations.idiomatic: She immediately halted the investigation, and Ruizong was saved.

sentences.zh: 當是時，朝廷士大夫翕然稱其誼，自以為弗及也。

translations.literal: At that time, court scholars and officials unanimously praised his righteousness and felt themselves unequal to him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time court officials unanimously praised his loyalty and felt they could not match him.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，母喪，葬南闕口，營石墳，晝夜不息。

translations.literal: Early in Shenlong, his mother died; he buried her at South Que Pass, constructing a stone tomb, working day and night without rest.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era, when his mother died, he buried her at South Que Pass and worked day and night without rest to build her stone tomb.

sentences.zh: 地本卬燥，泉忽湧流廬之側，李冬有華，犬鹿相擾。

translations.literal: The ground was originally high and dry; a spring suddenly gushed beside the hut; in late winter flowers bloomed; dogs and deer mingled together.
translations.idiomatic: Though the ground was originally dry and elevated, a spring suddenly gushed beside the mourning hut; flowers bloomed in late winter, and dogs and deer wandered together.

sentences.zh: 本道使盧懷慎上其事，詔表闕於閭。

translations.literal: The circuit commissioner Lu Huai-shen reported the matter; an edict erected a commemorative gate in the village.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit Commissioner Lu Huai-shen reported the matter, and an edict ordered a commemorative gate erected in the village.

sentences.zh: 景雲時，遷右武衛中郎將。

translations.literal: During Jingyun, transferred to Captain of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyun era he was promoted to Captain of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 玄宗屬其事於史官，擢右驍衛將軍，爵代國公。

translations.literal: Xuanzong entrusted the affair to the historiographers; he was promoted to General of the Right Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong had the historians record his deed; Jinzang was promoted to General of the Right Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Dai.

sentences.zh: 詔镵其名於泰、華二山碑以為榮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his name carved on the monuments of Mount Tai and Mount Hua as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his name carved on the monuments of Mount Tai and Mount Hua as an honor.

sentences.zh: 卒，配饗睿宗廟廷。

translations.literal: He died; his spirit tablet was placed in Ruizong's temple hall for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was granted a place in the sacrifices at Ruizong's temple.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，贈兵部尚書，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: During Dali, posthumously made Minister of War; posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era he was posthumously appointed Minister of War and given the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 以子承恩為廬州長史。

translations.literal: His son Chengen was made Chief Administrator of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengen was appointed Chief Administrator of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 中和中，又擢其遠孫敬則為太子右諭德。

translations.literal: During Zhonghe, his distant descendant Jingze was further promoted to Right Mentor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhonghe era his distant descendant Jingze was promoted to Right Mentor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 王同皎，相州安陽人，陳駙馬都尉寬曾孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Tongjiao, a native of Anyang in Xiangzhou, was the great-grandson of Kuan, Commandant of Chariots and Cavalry of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tongjiao was a native of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture and the great-grandson of Kuan, Commandant of Chariots and Cavalry of Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，徙河北。

translations.literal: When Chen perished, the family was relocated to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen dynasty fell, the family was relocated to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 長安中，尚太子女安定郡主，拜典膳郎。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era, he married the Crown Prince's daughter, Princess of Anding, and was appointed Master of Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era he married the Crown Prince's daughter, Princess of Anding, and was appointed Master of Provisions.

sentences.zh: 太子，中宗也。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince was Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince was Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 桓彥範等誅二張，遣同皎與李湛、李多祚即東宮迎太子，請至玄武門指授諸將。

translations.literal: Huan Yanfan and others executed the Two Zhangs; they sent Tongjiao with Li Zhan and Li Duozuo to the Eastern Palace to welcome the Crown Prince, requesting he come to the Xuanwu Gate to direct the generals.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Yanfan and others executed the Two Zhangs, they sent Tongjiao with Li Zhan and Li Duozuo to the Eastern Palace to fetch the Crown Prince and asked him to come to the Xuanwu Gate to direct the generals.

sentences.zh: 太子拒不許，同皎進曰：「逆豎反道，顯肆不軌，諸將與衙執事刻期誅之，須殿下到以系眾望。」

translations.literal: The Crown Prince refused to consent; Tongjiao advanced and said: "The rebellious villains oppose the Way and openly commit lawless acts; the generals and palace officials have set a date to execute them — we need Your Highness to come to bind the people's hopes."
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince refused; Tongjiao pressed him: "These traitors violate all propriety; the generals and palace officials have set a date to execute them — we need Your Highness to come and rally the people's hopes."

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「上方不豫，得無不可乎？」

translations.literal: The Crown Prince said: "The Emperor above is unwell — would it not be impermissible?"
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince said: "The Emperor is ill — would that not be improper?"

sentences.zh: 同皎曰：「南將相毀家族以安社稷，奈何欲內之鼎鑊乎？

translations.literal: Tongjiao said: "Southern ministers and generals have destroyed their own clans to secure the state — how can you wish to cast them into the cauldron?
translations.idiomatic: Tongjiao said: "Southern ministers and generals have destroyed their own families to save the realm — how can you mean to throw them into the executioner's cauldron?

sentences.zh: 太子能自出諭之，眾乃止。」

translations.literal: If the Crown Prince would come out himself to instruct them, the crowd would then stop."
translations.idiomatic: If the Crown Prince would come out himself to reassure them, the crowd would stop."

sentences.zh: 太子猶豫，同皎即扶上馬，從至玄武門，斬關入。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince hesitated; Tongjiao immediately helped him mount a horse, accompanied him to the Xuanwu Gate, cut through the gate, and entered.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince hesitated; Tongjiao immediately helped him onto a horse, accompanied him to the Xuanwu Gate, cut through the barrier, and entered.

sentences.zh: 兵趨長生殿太后所，環侍嚴定，因奏誅易之等狀。

translations.literal: The troops rushed to the Chamber of Everlasting Life where the Empress Dowager was, encircled her in a tight guard, and reported the grounds for executing Yizhi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The troops rushed to the Chamber of Everlasting Life where the Empress Dowager was, formed a tight ring around her, and reported the grounds for executing Zhang Yizhi and the others.

sentences.zh: 帝復位，擢右千牛將軍，封瑯邪公，食實戶五百。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was restored to the throne, Tongjiao was promoted to Right General of the Thousand-Ox Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Langya, with five hundred households as his fief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor was restored to the throne, Tongjiao was promoted to Right General of the Thousand-Ox Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Langya, with five hundred households as his fief.

sentences.zh: 主進封公主，拜同皎駙馬都尉，遷光祿卿。

translations.literal: The princess was elevated to full princess rank; Tongjiao was appointed Commandant of Horse in Attendance and promoted to Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was elevated to full princess rank; Tongjiao was appointed Commandant of Horse in Attendance to the Emperor and promoted to Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 神龍後，武三思烝濁王室，同皎惡之，與張仲之、祖延慶、周憬、李悛、冉祖雍謀，須武后靈駕發，伏弩射殺三思。

translations.literal: After Shenlong, Wu Sansi committed incest and corrupted the royal house; Tongjiao hated him and conspired with Zhang Zhongzhi, Zu Yanqing, Zhou Jing, Li Quan, and Ran Zuyong to ambush and shoot Sansi with crossbows when Empress Wu's funeral procession departed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shenlong coup, Wu Sansi committed incest and corrupted the imperial house; Tongjiao despised him and conspired with Zhang Zhongzhi, Zu Yanqing, Zhou Jing, Li Quan, and Ran Zuyong to lie in wait with crossbows and kill Sansi when Empress Wu's funeral procession set out.

sentences.zh: 會播州司兵參軍宋之愻以外妹妻延慶，延慶辭，之愻固請，乃成昏。

translations.literal: It happened that Song Zhixun, Staff Officer of Bozhou, sought to marry his younger cousin by marriage to Yanqing; Yanqing declined, but Zhixun pressed the matter until the marriage was made.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhixun, a staff officer in Bozhou, sought to marry his younger cousin by marriage to Yanqing; Yanqing declined, but Zhixun pressed the matter until the marriage was made.

sentences.zh: 延慶心厚之，不復疑。

translations.literal: Yanqing came to trust him deeply and no longer harbored suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing came to trust him deeply and no longer harbored any suspicion.

sentences.zh: 故之愻子曇得其實。

translations.literal: Thus Zhixun's son Tan learned the truth of the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zhixun's son Tan learned the truth of the plot.

sentences.zh: 之愻兄之問嘗舍仲之家，亦得其謀。

translations.literal: Zhixun's elder brother Zhiwen had once lodged at Zhongzhi's house and also learned of the conspiracy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun's elder brother Zhiwen had once lodged at Zhongzhi's house and also learned of the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 令曇密語三思。

translations.literal: They had Tan secretly inform Sansi.
translations.idiomatic: They had Tan secretly inform Sansi.

sentences.zh: 三思遣悛上急變，且言同皎欲擁兵闕下廢皇后。

translations.literal: Sansi sent Quan to report an urgent crisis, saying also that Tongjiao intended to gather troops below the palace gate to depose the Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi sent Quan to report an urgent crisis, claiming also that Tongjiao intended to gather troops below the palace gate to depose the Empress.

sentences.zh: 帝殊不曉，大怒，斬同皎於都亭驛，籍其家。

translations.literal: The Emperor utterly failed to understand and flew into a rage; Tongjiao was executed at Duyang Station and his household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor completely failed to understand and flew into a rage; Tongjiao was executed at Duyang Station and his household was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 同皎且死，神色自如。

translations.literal: As Tongjiao faced death, his expression remained composed.
translations.idiomatic: Even as Tongjiao faced death, his expression remained composed.

sentences.zh: 仲之、延慶皆死。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi and Yanqing were both executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi and Yanqing were both executed.

sentences.zh: 憬遁入比幹廟自剄，將死，謂人曰：「比幹，古忠臣，神而聰明，其知我乎！

translations.literal: Jing fled into the Temple of Bi Gan and slit his own throat; as he was dying, he said to those present: "Bi Gan was an ancient loyal minister, divine and perceptive — will he know me?
translations.idiomatic: Jing fled into the Temple of Bi Gan and slit his own throat; as he was dying, he said to those present: "Bi Gan was an ancient loyal minister, divine and perceptive — will he know me?

sentences.zh: 後、三思亂朝，虐害忠良，滅亡不久，可幹吾頭國門，見其敗也。」

translations.literal: The Empress and Sansi throw the court into chaos and cruelly harm the loyal and good; their destruction is not far off — you may hang my head at the national gate and witness their downfall."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress and Sansi throw the court into chaos and cruelly harm the loyal and good; their destruction is not far off — hang my head at the national gate and witness their downfall."

sentences.zh: 憬，壽春人。

translations.literal: Jing was a native of Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was a native of Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 後太子重俊誅三思，天下共傷同皎之不及見也。

translations.literal: Later, when Crown Prince Chongjun executed Sansi, the realm collectively mourned that Tongjiao had not lived to see it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Crown Prince Chongjun executed Sansi, the realm collectively mourned that Tongjiao had not lived to see it.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，詔復官爵，謚曰忠壯。

translations.literal: When Ruizong ascended the throne, an edict restored Tongjiao's offices and titles; his posthumous name was Loyal and Valiant.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong ascended the throne, an edict restored Tongjiao's offices and titles and gave him the posthumous name Loyal and Valiant.

sentences.zh: 誅祖雍、悛等。

translations.literal: Zuyong, Quan, and the others were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyong, Quan, and the others were executed.

sentences.zh: 先是，許州司戶參軍燕欽融再上書斥韋后擅政，且逆節已萌。

translations.literal: Previously, Yan Qinrong, Registrar of Xuzhou, had submitted memorials twice denouncing Empress Wei's seizure of power and warning that treason was already stirring.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Yan Qinrong, a registrar in Xu Prefecture, had submitted memorials twice denouncing Empress Wei's seizure of power and warning that treason was already stirring.

sentences.zh: 後怒，勸中宗召至廷，撲殺之。

translations.literal: The Empress was enraged and persuaded Zhongzong to summon him to court, where he was beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress was enraged and persuaded Zhongzong to summon him to court, where he was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 宗楚客復私令衛士極力，故死。

translations.literal: Zong Chuke privately ordered the guards to exert maximum force, which is why he died.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke privately ordered the guards to exert maximum force, which is why he died.

sentences.zh: 又博陵人郎岌亦表後及楚客亂，被誅。

translations.literal: Lang Ji of Boling also submitted a memorial accusing the Empress and Chuke of treason and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Ji of Boling also submitted a memorial accusing the Empress and Chuke of treason and was executed.

sentences.zh: 至是，俱贈諫議大夫，備禮改葬，賜欽融一子官。

translations.literal: At this point both were posthumously granted the post of Remonstrance and Reproof Minister, given full funeral rites and reburial, and Qinrong's son was granted an official post.
translations.idiomatic: At this point both were posthumously granted the post of Remonstrance and Reproof Minister, given full funeral rites and reburial, and one of Qinrong's sons was granted an official post.

sentences.zh: 同皎子繇尚永穆公主，生子潛，字弘誌。

translations.literal: Tongjiao's son You married Princess Yongmu and fathered Qian, styled Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Tongjiao's son You married Princess Yongmu and fathered Qian, styled Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 生三日，賜緋衣、銀魚。

translations.literal: On the third day after his birth, he was bestowed crimson robes and a silver fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day after his birth, he was bestowed crimson robes and a silver fish tally.

sentences.zh: 幼莊重，不喜兒弄。

translations.literal: From childhood he was dignified and sober, with no taste for childish play.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was dignified and sober, with no taste for childish play.

sentences.zh: 以帝外孫，補千牛，復選尚公主，固辭。

translations.literal: As the Emperor's grandson-in-law, he was appointed to the Thousand-Ox Guard; he was again selected to marry a princess but firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: As the Emperor's grandson-in-law, he was appointed to the Thousand-Ox Guard; he was again selected to marry a princess but firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 元和中擢累將作監。

translations.literal: During the Yuanhe era he was repeatedly promoted, eventually reaching Director of Works.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era he was repeatedly promoted, eventually reaching Director of Works.

sentences.zh: 吏或籍名北軍，輒驕墯不事，潛悉奏罷之，故不戒而辨。

translations.literal: Some subordinates whose names appeared on Northern Army rolls grew arrogant and slacked in their duties; Qian had them all dismissed by memorial, and matters were handled without prior warning or difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Some subordinates whose names appeared on Northern Army rolls grew arrogant and slacked in their duties; Qian had them all dismissed by memorial, and matters were handled without prior warning or difficulty.

sentences.zh: 監無公食，而息錢舊皆私有，至潛，取以具食，遂為故事。

translations.literal: The office had no official provisions, and interest payments had traditionally been kept private; under Qian they were used for communal meals, and this became the established practice.
translations.idiomatic: The office had no official provisions, and interest payments had traditionally been kept private; under Qian they were used for communal meals, and this became the established practice.

sentences.zh: 遷左散騎常侍，拜涇原節度使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and appointed Military Commissioner of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and appointed Military Commissioner of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 憲宗與對，大悅，曰：「吾知而善職，我自用之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong met with him and was greatly pleased, saying: "I know you excel at your duties — I shall employ you myself."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong met with him and was greatly pleased, saying: "I know you excel at your duties — I shall employ you myself."

sentences.zh: 潛至鎮，繕壁壘，積粟，構高屋偫兵，利而嚴。

translations.literal: When Qian arrived at his post, he repaired ramparts, stockpiled grain, built high structures to store arms, and made the prefecture both prosperous and strict.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian arrived at his post, he repaired ramparts, stockpiled grain, built high structures to store arms, and made the prefecture both prosperous and strict.

sentences.zh: 遂引師自原州逾硤石，取虜將一人，斥烽候，築歸化、潘原三壘。

translations.literal: He then led troops from Yuanzhou across Shimeng Pass, captured one enemy officer, drove back the beacon-guards, and built three fortresses at Guihua and Panyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then led troops from Yuan Prefecture across Shimeng Pass, captured one enemy officer, drove back the beacon-guards, and built three fortresses at Guihua and Panyuan.

sentences.zh: 請復城原州，度支沮議，故原州復陷。

translations.literal: He requested that Yuanzhou be fortified again, but the Board of Revenue blocked the proposal, and Yuanzhou fell once more.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that Yuan Prefecture be fortified again, but the Board of Revenue blocked the proposal, and Yuan Prefecture fell once more.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，封瑯邪郡公，更節度荊南。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Qian was enfeoffed as Duke of Langya and transferred to serve as Military Commissioner of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Qian was enfeoffed as Duke of Langya and transferred to serve as Military Commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 疏吏惡，榜之里閭，殺尤縱者。

translations.literal: He posted notices of official misconduct in the wards and executed the worst offenders.
translations.idiomatic: He posted notices of official misconduct in the wards and executed the worst offenders.

sentences.zh: 分射三等，課士習之，不能者罷，故無冗軍。

translations.literal: He divided archery into three grades, trained the soldiers accordingly, and dismissed those who could not meet the standard, so there were no superfluous troops.
translations.idiomatic: He divided archery into three grades, trained the soldiers accordingly, and dismissed those who could not meet the standard, so there were no superfluous troops.

sentences.zh: 大和初，檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the early Dahe era he was appointed acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Dahe era he was appointed acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，贈司空。

translations.literal: He died in office and was posthumously granted the title Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously granted the title Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 吳保安字永固，魏州從。

translations.literal: Wu Bao'an, styled Yonggu, was from Cong in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Bao'an, styled Yonggu, was from Cong in Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 氣挺特不俗。

translations.literal: His bearing was upright and out of the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was upright and out of the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 睿宗時，姚、巂蠻叛，拜李蒙為姚州都督，宰相郭元振以弟之子仲翔托蒙，蒙表為判官。

translations.literal: During Ruizong's reign, when the Yao and Xi tribes rebelled, Li Meng was appointed Prefect-General of Yaozhou; the Chief Minister Guo Yuanzhen entrusted his younger brother's son Zhongxiang to Meng, who recommended him as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: During Ruizong's reign, when the Yao and Xi tribes rebelled, Li Meng was appointed Prefect-General of Yao Prefecture; the Chief Minister Guo Yuanzhen entrusted his younger brother's son Zhongxiang to Meng, who recommended him as administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 時保安罷義安尉，未得調，以仲翔里人也，不介而見曰：「願因子得事李將軍可乎？」

translations.literal: At the time Bao'an had left his post as Captain of Yi'an and had not yet received a new appointment; as a fellow townsman of Zhongxiang, he came unintroduced and said: "Might I serve General Li through you?"
translations.idiomatic: At the time Bao'an had left his post as Captain of Yi'an and had not yet received a new appointment; as a fellow townsman of Zhongxiang, he came unintroduced and said: "Might I serve General Li through you?"

sentences.zh: 仲翔雖無雅故，哀其窮，力薦之。

translations.literal: Although Zhongxiang had no prior acquaintance with him, he was moved by Bao'an's plight and vigorously recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Although Zhongxiang had no prior acquaintance with him, he was moved by Bao'an's plight and vigorously recommended him.

sentences.zh: 蒙表掌書記。

translations.literal: Meng appointed him Recorder of Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Meng appointed him Recorder of Documents.

sentences.zh: 保安後往，蒙已深入，與蠻戰沒，仲翔被執。

translations.literal: Bao'an arrived later; Meng had already advanced deep into the territory and perished in battle with the tribes, and Zhongxiang was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Bao'an arrived later; Meng had already advanced deep into the territory and perished in battle with the tribes, and Zhongxiang was captured.

sentences.zh: 蠻之俘華人，必厚責財，乃肯贖，聞仲翔貴胄也，求千縑。

translations.literal: When the tribes captured Chinese subjects, they always demanded a heavy ransom before releasing them; learning that Zhongxiang was of noble birth, they demanded a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes captured Chinese subjects, they always demanded a heavy ransom before releasing them; learning that Zhongxiang was of noble birth, they demanded a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 會元振物故，保安留巂州，營贖仲翔，苦無貲。

translations.literal: When Yuanzhen died, Bao'an remained in Xi Prefecture and worked to ransom Zhongxiang, but had no funds.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanzhen died, Bao'an remained in Xi Prefecture and worked to ransom Zhongxiang, but had no funds.

sentences.zh: 乃力居貨十年，得縑七百。

translations.literal: He toiled at trade for ten years and accumulated seven hundred bolts.
translations.idiomatic: He toiled at trade for ten years and accumulated seven hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 妻子客遂州，間關求保安所在，困姚州不能進。

translations.literal: His wife and dependents stayed in Suizhou and made their way arduously to find Bao'an, but were stranded in Yaozhou and could not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and dependents stayed in Sui Prefecture and made their way arduously to find Bao'an, but were stranded in Yao Prefecture and could not proceed.

sentences.zh: 都督楊安居知狀，異其故，資以行，求保安得之。

translations.literal: Prefect Yang Anju learned of the situation, marveled at the reason, and financed their journey; they found Bao'an.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Yang Anju learned of the situation, marveled at the reason, and financed their journey; they found Bao'an.

sentences.zh: 引與語曰：「子棄家急朋友之患至是乎！

translations.literal: Anju took him aside and said: "You abandoned your family in urgent loyalty to a friend — has it come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Anju took him aside and said: "You abandoned your family in urgent loyalty to a friend — has it come to this?

sentences.zh: 吾請貣官貲助子之乏。」

translations.literal: I shall advance you official funds to make up what you lack."
translations.idiomatic: I shall advance you official funds to make up what you lack."

sentences.zh: 保安大喜，即委縑於蠻，得仲翔以歸。

translations.literal: Bao'an was overjoyed and immediately delivered the silk to the tribes, obtained Zhongxiang, and brought him home.
translations.idiomatic: Bao'an was overjoyed and immediately delivered the silk to the tribes, obtained Zhongxiang, and brought him home.

sentences.zh: 始，仲翔為蠻所奴，三逃三獲，乃轉鬻遠酋，酋嚴遇之，晝役夜囚，沒凡十五年乃還。

translations.literal: At first Zhongxiang had been enslaved by the tribes; he escaped three times and was recaptured three times, then was sold on to a distant chieftain who treated him harshly — by day he labored, by night he was imprisoned — and altogether spent fifteen years in captivity before returning.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhongxiang had been enslaved by the tribes; he escaped three times and was recaptured three times, then was sold on to a distant chieftain who treated him harshly — by day he labored, by night he was imprisoned — and altogether spent fifteen years in captivity before returning.

sentences.zh: 安居亦丞相故吏，嘉保安之誼，厚禮仲翔，遺衣服儲用，檄領近縣尉。

translations.literal: Anju was also a former subordinate of the Chief Minister; admiring Bao'an's loyalty, he treated Zhongxiang generously, gave him clothes and supplies, and had him appointed district captain of a nearby county.
translations.idiomatic: Anju was also a former subordinate of the Chief Minister; admiring Bao'an's loyalty, he treated Zhongxiang generously, gave him clothes and supplies, and had him appointed district captain of a nearby county.

sentences.zh: 久乃調蔚州錄事參軍，以優遷代州戶曹。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Registrar of Weizhou and, through excellent performance, promoted to Census Officer of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was transferred to Registrar of Wei Prefecture and, through excellent performance, promoted to Census Officer of Dai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 母喪，服除，喟曰：「吾賴吳公生吾死，今親歿，可行其志。」

translations.literal: When his mother's mourning was finished, he sighed: "My life and death depend on Wu Gong — now that my parents are gone, I can fulfill my purpose."
translations.idiomatic: When his mother's mourning was finished, he sighed: "My life and death depend on Wu Gong — now that my parents are gone, I can fulfill my purpose."

sentences.zh: 乃求保安。

translations.literal: He then sought out Bao'an.
translations.idiomatic: He then sought out Bao'an.

sentences.zh: 於時，何安以彭山丞客死，其妻亦沒，喪不克歸。

translations.literal: At that time He An, a Pengshan assistant magistrate, had died away from home as a guest, and his wife was also lost; their remains could not be returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At that time He An, a Pengshan assistant magistrate, had died away from home as a guest, and his wife was also lost; their remains could not be returned home.

sentences.zh: 仲翔為服缞绖，囊其骨，徒跣負之，歸葬魏州，廬墓三年乃去。

translations.literal: Zhongxiang wore mourning garments, wrapped the bones in a bag, went barefoot carrying them on his back, returned them to Weizhou for burial, and kept vigil at the tomb for three years before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiang wore mourning garments, wrapped the bones in a bag, went barefoot carrying them on his back, returned them to Wei Prefecture for burial, and kept vigil at the tomb for three years before leaving.

sentences.zh: 後為嵐州長史，迎保安子，為娶而讓以官。

translations.literal: Later, as Chief Administrator of Lan Prefecture, he welcomed Bao'an's son, married him to a wife, and yielded his own official position to him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Chief Administrator of Lan Prefecture, he welcomed Bao'an's son, married him to a wife, and yielded his own official position to him.

sentences.zh: 李憕，并州汶水人。

translations.literal: Li Xian was a native of Wenshui in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian was a native of Wenshui in Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 或言其先出興聖皇帝，譜系疏晦，不復傳。

translations.literal: Some said his ancestors descended from the Emperor of Sagely Origin, but the genealogy was obscure and no longer transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Some said his ancestors descended from the Emperor of Sagely Origin, but the genealogy was obscure and no longer transmitted.

sentences.zh: 父希倩，神龍初右臺監察御史。

translations.literal: His father Xiqian was a Supervising Censor of the Right Bureau during the Shenlong era.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiqian was a Supervising Censor of the Right Bureau during the Shenlong era.

sentences.zh: 憕少秀敏，舉明經高第，授成安尉。

translations.literal: Xian was exceptionally gifted from youth; he passed the Classics examination with high honors and was appointed Captain of Cheng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was exceptionally gifted from youth; he passed the Classics examination with high honors and was appointed Captain of Cheng'an.

sentences.zh: 張說罷宰相，為相州刺史，坐有善相者，說遍問官屬後孰當貴，工指憕及臨河尉鄭巖。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yue was dismissed as Chief Minister and made Prefect of Xiangzhou, because he had a skilled physiognomist with him, he asked all his subordinates who would later become eminent; the artisan pointed to Xian and Zheng Yan, captain of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yue was dismissed as Chief Minister and made Prefect of Xiang Prefecture, because he had a skilled physiognomist with him, he asked all his subordinates who would later become eminent; the artisan pointed to Xian and Zheng Yan, captain of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 說以女妻巖，而歸其甥陰於憕。

translations.literal: Yue gave his daughter to Yan in marriage and entrusted his nephew Yin to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Yue gave his daughter to Yan in marriage and entrusted his nephew Yin to Xian.

sentences.zh: 會母喪免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed when his mother died.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 自武功尉以政尤異遷主簿。

translations.literal: From Captain of Wugong he was promoted to Chief Clerk for outstanding administration.
translations.idiomatic: From Captain of Wugong he was promoted to Chief Clerk for outstanding administration.

sentences.zh: 說在并州，引憕置幕府。

translations.literal: When Yue was in Bingzhou, he recruited Xian into his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue was in Bing Prefecture, he recruited Xian into his staff.

sentences.zh: 及執政，為長安尉。

translations.literal: When Yue took power at court, Xian became Captain of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue took power at court, Xian became Captain of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 宇文融括天下田，高選官屬，多致賢以重其柄。

translations.literal: Yuwen Rong registered all land in the empire and sought highly capable staff; he brought in many able men to strengthen his authority.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Rong registered all land in the empire and sought highly capable staff; he brought in many able men to strengthen his authority.

sentences.zh: 表假憕監察御史，分道檢核。

translations.literal: He memorialized to borrow Xian as Supervising Censor to inspect and verify land on separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to borrow Xian as Supervising Censor to inspect and verify land on separate routes.

sentences.zh: 以課真拜御史。

translations.literal: For the thoroughness of his investigations he was appointed censor in fact.
translations.idiomatic: For the thoroughness of his investigations he was appointed censor in fact.

sentences.zh: 坐小累，下除晉陽令。

translations.literal: For a minor fault he was demoted to Magistrate of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: For a minor fault he was demoted to Magistrate of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 三遷給事中。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Recipient of Petitions.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became Recipient of Petitions.

sentences.zh: 力於治，有任事稱，明簿最，下無敢紿。

translations.literal: He was vigorous in administration and had a reputation for handling affairs; he knew registers and regulations precisely, and subordinates dared not deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: He was vigorous in administration and had a reputation for handling affairs; he knew registers and regulations precisely, and subordinates dared not deceive him.

sentences.zh: 失李林甫意，出為河南少尹。

translations.literal: He lost Li Linfu's favor and was sent out as Vice Director of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He lost Li Linfu's favor and was sent out as Vice Director of Henan.

sentences.zh: 尹蕭炅內倚權，骫法殖私，憕裁抑其謬，吏下賴之。

translations.literal: Vice Director Xiao Jiong relied on powerful patrons and bent the law for private gain; Xian checked his errors, and the officials below relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Xiao Jiong relied on powerful patrons and bent the law for private gain; Xian checked his errors, and the officials below relied on him.

sentences.zh: 道士孫甑生以左道幸，托祠事往來嵩、少間，幹請亂吏治，憕不為應，故挾炅譖諸朝。

translations.literal: The Daoist Sun Zansheng, favored for heterodox arts, used temple rites as a pretext to travel between Mount Song and Mount Shao soliciting favors and corrupting administration; Xian would not comply, so he joined with Jiong to slander Xian at court.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Sun Zansheng, favored for heterodox arts, used temple rites as a pretext to travel between Mount Song and Mount Shao soliciting favors and corrupting administration; Xian would not comply, so he joined with Jiong to slander Xian at court.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，除清河太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianbao era he was appointed Prefect of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianbao era he was appointed Prefect of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 舉美政，遷廣陵長史，民為立祠賽祝，歲時不絕。

translations.literal: For excellent governance he was promoted to Chief Administrator of Guangling; the people built a shrine for him and offered sacrifices without cease through the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: For excellent governance he was promoted to Chief Administrator of Guangling; the people built a shrine for him and offered sacrifices without cease through the seasons.

sentences.zh: 以捕賊負，徙彭城太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Pengcheng for failing to capture bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Prefect of Pengcheng for failing to capture bandits.

sentences.zh: 封酒泉縣侯。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 連徙襄陽、河東，並兼采訪處置使；

translations.literal: He was transferred successively to Xiangyang and Hedong, in each case also serving as Investigation and Disposition Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred successively to Xiangyang and Hedong, in each case also serving as Investigation and Disposition Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入為京兆尹。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Intendant of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠惡之，改光祿卿、東京留守。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong hated him and had him made Director of the Imperial Household and Keeper of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong hated him and had him made Director of the Imperial Household and Keeper of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，玄宗遣封常清募兵東京，憕與留臺御史中丞盧弈、河南尹達奚珣繕城壘，綏勵士卒，將遏賊西鋒。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Emperor Xuanzong dispatched Feng Changqing to recruit troops in the Eastern Capital; Xian, together with Left Deputy Censor Lu Yi and Henan Vice Director Daxi Xun, repaired the city walls, encouraged the soldiers, and prepared to block the rebels' westward thrust.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Emperor Xuanzong dispatched Feng Changqing to recruit troops in the Eastern Capital; Xian, together with Left Deputy Censor Lu Yi and Henan Vice Director Daxi Xun, repaired the city walls, encouraged the soldiers, and prepared to block the rebels' westward thrust.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，擢禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of this, he promoted Xian to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard of this, he promoted Xian to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 祿山度河，號令嚴密，候诇不能知。

translations.literal: Lushan crossed the Yellow River; his orders were strict and scouts could not detect his movements.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan crossed the Yellow River; his orders were strict and scouts could not detect his movements.

sentences.zh: 已陷陳留、滎陽，殺張介然、崔诐，不數日，薄城下。

translations.literal: Chenliu and Xingyang had already fallen; Zhang Jieran and Cui Qian were killed; within days the rebels pressed beneath the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Chenliu and Xingyang had already fallen; Zhang Jieran and Cui Qian were killed; within days the rebels pressed beneath the city walls.

sentences.zh: 常清兵皆白徒，戰不勝，輒北。

translations.literal: Changqing's troops were all raw recruits; when they fought they could not win and always fled north.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing's troops were all raw recruits; when they fought they could not win and always fled north.

sentences.zh: 憕收殘士數百，裒斷弦折矢堅守，人不堪鬥。

translations.literal: Xian gathered several hundred survivors, collected broken strings and snapped arrows, and held a stubborn defense; the men could no longer bear to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Xian gathered several hundred survivors, collected broken strings and snapped arrows, and held a stubborn defense; the men could no longer bear to fight.

sentences.zh: 憕約弈：「吾曹荷國重寄，雖力不敵，當死官。」

translations.literal: Xian made a pact with Yi: "We bear a heavy charge from the state; though our strength is insufficient, we must die at our posts."
translations.idiomatic: Xian made a pact with Yi: "We bear a heavy charge from the state; though our strength is insufficient, we must die at our posts."

sentences.zh: 部校皆夜縋去，憕坐留守府，弈守臺。

translations.literal: That night all the unit commanders lowered themselves by rope and fled; Xian remained at the Keeper's headquarters while Yi held the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: That night all the unit commanders lowered themselves by rope and fled; Xian remained at the Keeper's headquarters while Yi held the censorate.

sentences.zh: 城陷，祿山鼓而入，殺數千人，矢著闕門，執憕、弈及官屬蔣清，害之。

translations.literal: The city fell; Lushan beat his drums and entered, killing several thousand men; arrows struck the palace gate; Xian, Yi, and the official Jiang Qing were seized and put to death.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell; Lushan beat his drums and entered, killing several thousand men; arrows struck the palace gate; Xian, Yi, and the official Jiang Qing were seized and put to death

sentences.zh: 有詔贈司徒，謚曰忠懿。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him the title of Grand Mentor and gave him the posthumous name Loyal and Benevolent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously granted him the title of Grand Mentor and gave him the posthumous name Loyal and Benevolent

sentences.zh: 河、洛平，再贈太尉，拜一子五品官。

translations.literal: When the Yellow and Luo regions were pacified, he was again posthumously made Grand Marshal and one of his sons was granted a fifth-rank official post.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow and Luo regions were pacified, he was again posthumously made Grand Marshal and one of his sons was granted a fifth-rank official post

sentences.zh: 憕通《左氏春秋》，頗殖產伊川，占膏腴，自都至闕口，疇墅彌望，時謂「地癖」。

translations.literal: Xian was versed in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and greatly accumulated property in Yichuan, seizing fertile land; from the capital to the Pass mouth, fields and villas stretched as far as the eye could see, and at the time he was called a "land fanatic.".
translations.idiomatic: Xian was versed in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and greatly accumulated property in Yichuan, seizing fertile land; from the capital to the Pass mouth, fields and villas stretched as far as the eye could see, and at the time he was called a "land fanatic."

sentences.zh: 巖仕終少府監，產利埒憕雲。

translations.literal: Yan served to the end as Director of the Palace Workshop, and his wealth rivaled Xian's.
translations.idiomatic: Yan served to the end as Director of the Palace Workshop, and his wealth rivaled Xian's

sentences.zh: 憕十餘子，江、涵、沨、瀛等同遇害，唯源、彭脫。

translations.literal: Xian had more than ten sons; Jiang, Han, Feng, and Ying were killed along with him, but only Yuan and Peng escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had more than ten sons; Jiang, Han, Feng, and Ying were killed along with him, but only Yuan and Peng escaped

sentences.zh: 源八歲家覆，俘為奴，轉側民間。

translations.literal: Yuan was eight when his family was destroyed; he was captured and made a slave, passing from household to household.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was eight when his family was destroyed; he was captured and made a slave, passing from household to household

sentences.zh: 及史朝義敗，故吏識源於洛陽者贖出之，歸其宗屬。

translations.literal: When Shi Chaoyi's forces were defeated, former subordinates who recognized Yuan in Luoyang ransomed him and returned him to his clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Chaoyi's forces were defeated, former subordinates who recognized Yuan in Luoyang ransomed him and returned him to his clan

sentences.zh: 代宗聞，授河南府參軍，遷司農主簿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong heard of this, he appointed Yuan as an aide in Henan Prefecture and later promoted him to Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong heard of this, he appointed Yuan as an aide in Henan Prefecture and later promoted him to Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Revenue

sentences.zh: 以父死賊手，常悲憤，不仕不娶，絕酒葷。

translations.literal: Because his father had died at the rebels' hands, he was constantly grief-stricken and angry; he would not take office or marry, and abstained from wine and meat.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had died at the rebels' hands, he was constantly grief-stricken and angry; he would not take office or marry, and abstained from wine and meat

sentences.zh: 惠林佛祠者，憕舊墅也，源依祠居，闔戶日一食。

translations.literal: The Huilin Buddhist temple was Xian's former villa; Yuan lived by the temple, closing his door and eating only once a day.
translations.idiomatic: The Huilin Buddhist temple was Xian's former villa; Yuan lived by the temple, closing his door and eating only once a day

sentences.zh: 祠殿，其先寢也，每過必趨，未始踐階。

translations.literal: The temple hall had been his father's sleeping quarters; whenever he passed it he would hasten his step and never tread upon the steps.
translations.idiomatic: The temple hall had been his father's sleeping quarters; whenever he passed it he would hasten his step and never tread upon the steps

sentences.zh: 自營墓為終制，時時偃臥埏中。

translations.literal: He prepared his own tomb as his final resting place and would often lie down within the burial mound.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared his own tomb as his final resting place and would often lie down within the burial mound

sentences.zh: 長慶初，年八十矣，御史中丞李德裕表薦源，曰：「賈誼稱：守圉捍敵之臣，死城郭封疆。

translations.literal: In the early Changqing era, when he was already eighty, Left Deputy Censor Li Deyu memorialized recommending Yuan, saying: "Jia Yi said: ministers who defend the realm and repel enemies die for city walls and frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Changqing era, when he was already eighty, Left Deputy Censor Li Deyu memorialized recommending Yuan, saying: "Jia Yi said: ministers who defend the realm and repel enemies die for city walls and frontiers

sentences.zh: 天寶時，士罕伏節，逆羯始興，委符組、棄城郭者不為恥，而憕約義同列，守位自如，抵刃就終，臣節之光由憕始。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, few scholars upheld their integrity; when the rebellious Jie first rose, those who cast aside their seals and abandoned their cities felt no shame, yet Xian pledged righteousness with his colleagues, held his post steadfastly, and met death at the blade — the brilliance of ministerial integrity began with Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era, few scholars upheld their integrity; when the rebellious Jie first rose, those who cast aside their seals and abandoned their cities felt no shame, yet Xian pledged righteousness with his colleagues, held his post steadfastly, and met death at the blade — the brilliance of ministerial integrity began with Xian

sentences.zh: 而源天與至孝，絕心祿仕五十餘年，常守沈默，理契深要，一辭開析，百慮洗然。

translations.literal: Yuan, endowed with supreme filial piety, renounced salary and office for more than fifty years, always keeping silent; his understanding matched profound essentials, and once he opened his mouth to explain a matter, a hundred confused thoughts were washed clean.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, endowed with supreme filial piety, renounced salary and office for more than fifty years, always keeping silent; his understanding matched profound essentials, and once he opened his mouth to explain a matter, a hundred confused thoughts were washed clean

sentences.zh: 抱此真節，棄於清世，臣竊為陛下惜之。」

translations.literal: Holding such genuine integrity yet cast aside in a clear age — your servant grieves for Your Majesty that this is so."
translations.idiomatic: Holding such genuine integrity yet cast aside in a clear age — your servant grieves for Your Majesty that this is so"

sentences.zh: 穆宗下詔曰：「昔盜起幽陵，振蕩河、洛，贈太尉憕處難居首，正色就死，兩河聞風，再固危壁，殊節卓焉，到今稱之。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong issued an edict saying: "In former days, when bandits rose in Youling and shook the Yellow and Luo, the posthumous Grand Marshal Xian stood foremost in adversity, met death with a stern countenance, and when the two river regions heard the wind, again fortified the perilous walls — his extraordinary integrity is praised to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong issued an edict saying: "In former days, when bandits rose in Youling and shook the Yellow and Luo, the posthumous Grand Marshal Xian stood foremost in adversity, met death with a stern countenance, and when the two river regions heard the wind, again fortified the perilous walls — his extraordinary integrity is praised to this day

sentences.zh: 源有曾參之行、巢父之操，泊然無營，汔此高年。

translations.literal: Yuan has the conduct of Zeng Shen and the integrity of Chao Fu; placid and without ambition, he has reached this advanced age.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan has the conduct of Zeng Shen and the integrity of Chao Fu; placid and without ambition, he has reached this advanced age

sentences.zh: 夫褒忠，所以勸臣節也；

translations.literal: To reward loyalty is to encourage ministerial integrity;.
translations.idiomatic: To reward loyalty is to encourage ministerial integrity;

sentences.zh: 旌孝，所以激人倫也；

translations.literal: to honor filial piety is to stir human relations;.
translations.idiomatic: to honor filial piety is to stir human relations;

sentences.zh: 鎮澆浮，莫如尚義；

translations.literal: to check frivolity and drift, nothing surpasses esteeming righteousness;.
translations.idiomatic: to check frivolity and drift, nothing surpasses esteeming righteousness;

sentences.zh: 厚風俗，莫如尊老。

translations.literal: to strengthen custom, nothing surpasses honoring the aged.
translations.idiomatic: to strengthen custom, nothing surpasses honoring the aged

sentences.zh: 舉是四者，大儆於時。

translations.literal: To advance these four is a great warning to the age.
translations.idiomatic: To advance these four is a great warning to the age

sentences.zh: 其以源守諫議大夫，賜緋魚袋。」

translations.literal: Let Yuan be appointed Remonstrance and Reproof Minister and granted crimson robes and a fish tally."
translations.idiomatic: Let Yuan be appointed Remonstrance and Reproof Minister and granted crimson robes and a fish tally."

sentences.zh: 河南尹遣官敦諭上道，帝自遣使者持詔書袍笏即賜，又賜絹二百匹。

translations.literal: The Intendant of Henan sent officials to urge him to take the road to court; the Emperor himself dispatched an envoy bearing the edict, robes, and tablet to bestow them, and also granted two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Intendant of Henan sent officials to urge him to take the road to court; the Emperor himself dispatched an envoy bearing the edict, robes, and tablet to bestow them, and also granted two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 源頓首受詔，謂使者：「伏疾年耄，不堪趨拜。」

translations.literal: Yuan bowed his head and received the edict, telling the envoy: "I lie ill with age and am unable to perform the court bow."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan bowed his head and received the edict, telling the envoy: "I lie ill with age and am unable to perform the court bow."

sentences.zh: 即附表謝，辭吐哀愨，一無受。

translations.literal: He immediately appended a memorial of thanks, its language mournful and sincere, and accepted nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately appended a memorial of thanks, its language mournful and sincere, and accepted nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died

sentences.zh: 敬宗時，擢憕孫為河南兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: During the Jingzong era, Xian's grandson was promoted to Military Staff Officer of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingzong era, Xian's grandson was promoted to Military Staff Officer of Henan

sentences.zh: 彭擢明經第。

translations.literal: Peng passed the Classics examination with high honors.
translations.idiomatic: Peng passed the Classics examination with high honors

sentences.zh: 天寶中，選名臣子可用者，自咸寧丞遷右補闕。

translations.literal: During the Tianbao era, when sons of eminent ministers who were fit for service were selected, he was transferred from Assistant Magistrate of Xianning to Right Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era, when sons of eminent ministers who were fit for service were selected, he was transferred from Assistant Magistrate of Xianning to Right Supplementation Censor

sentences.zh: 從天子入蜀。

translations.literal: He followed the Son of Heaven into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Son of Heaven into Shu

sentences.zh: 後憕數年卒。

translations.literal: He died several years after Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He died several years after Xian

sentences.zh: 有孫景讓、景莊、景溫，別傳。

translations.literal: He had grandsons Jingrang, Jingzhuang, and Jingwen, treated in separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: He had grandsons Jingrang, Jingzhuang, and Jingwen, treated in separate biographies

sentences.zh: 武德功臣十六人，貞觀功臣五十三人，至德功臣二百六十五人。

translations.literal: There were sixteen meritorious officials of the Wude era, fifty-three of the Zhenguan era, and two hundred sixty-five of the Zhide era.
translations.idiomatic: There were sixteen meritorious officials of the Wude era, fifty-three of the Zhenguan era, and two hundred sixty-five of the Zhide era

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，錄武德以來宰相及實封功臣子孫，賜一子正員官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong ascended the throne, he recorded the descendants of chief ministers and meritorious officials with actual fiefs since the Wude era and granted one of each a regular official post.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong ascended the throne, he recorded the descendants of chief ministers and meritorious officials with actual fiefs since the Wude era and granted one of each a regular official post

sentences.zh: 史館考勛名特高者九十二人，以三等條奏。

translations.literal: The History Office examined ninety-two persons whose meritorious names were especially eminent and submitted them in three grades.
translations.idiomatic: The History Office examined ninety-two persons whose meritorious names were especially eminent and submitted them in three grades

sentences.zh: 第一等，以其歲授官。

translations.literal: For the first grade, office was granted in that year.
translations.idiomatic: For the first grade, office was granted in that year

sentences.zh: 第二等，以次年。

translations.literal: For the second grade, in the following year.
translations.idiomatic: For the second grade, in the following year

sentences.zh: 第三等，子孫數訟於朝，有詔差為二等，增至百八十七人。

translations.literal: For the third grade, when descendants repeatedly petitioned at court, an edict adjusted them to the second grade, increasing the total to one hundred eighty-seven persons.
translations.idiomatic: For the third grade, when descendants repeatedly petitioned at court, an edict adjusted them to the second grade, increasing the total to one hundred eighty-seven persons

sentences.zh: 每等，武德以來宰相為首，功臣次之，至德以來將相又次之。

translations.literal: Within each grade, chief ministers since Wude came first, meritorious officials next, and generals and ministers since Zhide after that.
translations.idiomatic: Within each grade, chief ministers since Wude came first, meritorious officials next, and generals and ministers since Zhide after that

sentences.zh: 大中初，又詔求李峴、王珪、戴胄、馬周、褚遂良、韓瑗、郝處俊、婁師德、王及善、朱敬則、魏知古、陸象先、張九齡、裴寂、劉文靜、張柬之、袁恕已、崔玄暐、桓彥範、劉幽求、郭元振、房琯、寺履謙、李嗣業、張巡、許遠、盧弈、南霽雲、蕭華、張鎬、李勉、張鎰、蕭復、柳渾、賈耽、馬燧、李憕三十七人畫像，續圖淩煙閣雲。

translations.literal: In the early Dazhong era, an edict also sought portraits of thirty-seven men — Li Xian, Wang Gui, Dai Zhou, Ma Zhou, Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, Hao Chujun, Lou Shide, Wang Jishan, Zhu Jingze, Wei Zhigu, Lu Xiangxian, Zhang Jiuling, Pei Ji, Liu Wenjing, Zhang Jianzhi, Yuan Shuyi, Cui Xuanwei, Huan Yanfan, Liu Youqiu, Guo Yuanzhen, Fang Guan, Yuan Lüqian, Li Siye, Zhang Xun, Xu Yuan, Lu Yi, Nan Jiyun, Xiao Hua, Zhang Gao, Li Mian, Zhang Yi, Xiao Fu, Liu Hun, Jia Dan, Ma Sui, and Li Xian — to continue the portraits at the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Dazhong era, an edict also sought portraits of thirty-seven men — Li Xian, Wang Gui, Dai Zhou, Ma Zhou, Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, Hao Chujun, Lou Shide, Wang Jishan, Zhu Jingze, Wei Zhigu, Lu Xiangxian, Zhang Jiuling, Pei Ji, Liu Wenjing, Zhang Jianzhi, Yuan Shuyi, Cui Xuanwei, Huan Yanfan, Liu Youqiu, Guo Yuanzhen, Fang Guan, Yuan Lüqian, Li Siye, Zhang Xun, Xu Yuan, Lu Yi, Nan Jiyun, Xiao Hua, Zhang Gao, Li Mian, Zhang Yi, Xiao Fu, Liu Hun, Jia Dan, Ma Sui, and Li Xian — to continue the portraits at the Lingyan Pavilion

sentences.zh: 盧弈，黃門監懷慎少子也。

translations.literal: Lu Yi was the youngest son of Director of the Yellow Gate Lu Huaishen.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi was the youngest son of Yellow Gate Director Lu Huaishen.

sentences.zh: 疏眉目，豐下，謹重寡欲，斤斤自脩。

translations.literal: His features were fine and regular and his lower face full; he was cautious, restrained, and free of desire, meticulously disciplining himself.
translations.idiomatic: His features were fine and regular, his lower face full; he was cautious, restrained, and free of desire, and meticulously disciplined himself.

sentences.zh: 與兄奐名相上下，而剛毅過之。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Huan were equally renowned, yet he surpassed Huan in resoluteness.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Huan were equally renowned, but he surpassed Huan in resoluteness.

sentences.zh: 天寶初為鄠令，所治輒最，積功擢給事中，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the early Tianbao era he served as Magistrate of E Prefecture; wherever he governed he ranked first, and through accumulated merit he was promoted to Recipient of Petitions and appointed Deputy Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tianbao era he served as Magistrate of E Prefecture; wherever he governed he ranked first, and through accumulated merit he was promoted to Recipient of Petitions and appointed Deputy Censor-in-Chief

sentences.zh: 自懷慎、奐及弈，三居其官，清節似之，時傳其美。

translations.literal: From Huaishen and Huan down to Yi, three generations held that office; their integrity resembled his, and at the time their virtue was celebrated.
translations.idiomatic: From Huaishen and Huan down to Yi, three generations held that office; their integrity matched his, and at the time their virtue was celebrated.

sentences.zh: 俄留臺東都，兼知武部選。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was made Keeper of the Eastern Capital and concurrently directed military selection at the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Keeper of the Eastern Capital and concurrently directed military selection at the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 安祿山陷東都，吏亡散。

translations.literal: When An Lushan captured the Eastern Capital, the officials dispersed in flight.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan captured the Eastern Capital, the officials fled and scattered.

sentences.zh: 弈前遣妻子懷印間道走京師，自朝服坐臺。

translations.literal: Yi had previously sent his wife and children, carrying the seals, by a secret route to the capital; he himself sat at the censorate in court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had previously sent his wife and children, carrying the seals, by a secret route to the capital; he himself sat at the censorate in court dress.

sentences.zh: 被執，將殺之，即數祿山罪，徐顧賊徒曰：「為人臣者當識逆順，我不蹈失節，死何恨？」

translations.literal: Seized and about to be executed, he immediately enumerated Lushan's crimes and slowly turned to the rebel followers, saying: "As ministers we should know loyalty from treason; I have not failed in integrity — what regret is there in death?"
translations.idiomatic: Seized and about to be executed, he immediately enumerated Lushan's crimes and slowly turned to the rebel followers, saying: "As ministers we should know loyalty from treason; I have not failed in integrity — what regret is there in death?"

sentences.zh: 觀者恐懼。

translations.literal: The onlookers were terrified.
translations.idiomatic: The onlookers were terrified.

sentences.zh: 弈臨刑，西向再拜而辭，罵賊不空口，逆黨為變色。

translations.literal: As Yi faced execution, he bowed twice toward the west and took leave; he cursed the rebels without pause, and the traitors changed color.
translations.idiomatic: As Yi faced execution, he bowed twice toward the west and took leave; he cursed the rebels without pause, and the traitors changed color.

sentences.zh: 肅宗詔贈禮部尚書，下有司謚。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong issued an edict posthumously granting him the title of Minister of Rites and ordering the relevant offices to assign a posthumous name.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong issued an edict posthumously granting him the title of Minister of Rites and ordering the relevant offices to assign a posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 時以為洛陽亡，操兵者任其咎，執法吏去之可也，委身寇仇，以死誰懟？

translations.literal: At the time people thought that with Luoyang lost, those who wielded arms bore the blame and law-enforcement officials could simply withdraw — why entrust oneself to the enemy and die to no purpose?
translations.idiomatic: At the time people thought that with Luoyang lost, those who wielded arms bore the blame and law-enforcement officials could simply withdraw — why entrust oneself to the enemy and die to no purpose?

sentences.zh: 博士獨孤及曰：「荀息殺身於晉，不食其言也；

translations.literal: Erudite Dugu Ji said: "Xun Xi gave his life at Jin rather than break his word;
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Dugu Ji said: "Xun Xi gave his life at Jin rather than break his word;

sentences.zh: 玄冥勤其官水死，守位忘躬也；

translations.literal: Xuanming drowned in the water while diligently performing his office, forgetting himself in holding his post;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanming drowned in the water while diligently performing his office, forgetting himself in holding his post;

sentences.zh: 伯姬待姆而火死，先禮後身也。

translations.literal: Bo Ji waited for her nurse and died in the fire, putting ritual before her own body.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Ji waited for her nurse and died in the fire, putting ritual before her own body.

sentences.zh: 彼死之日，皆於事無補。

translations.literal: On the days they died, none of these acts was of practical benefit.
translations.idiomatic: On the days they died, none of these acts was of practical benefit.

sentences.zh: 然則祿山亂大於裏、丕，弈廉察之任，切於玄冥之官。

translations.literal: Yet Lushan's rebellion was greater than the disorders of Li and Pi, and Yi's duty of integrity and investigation was more urgent than Xuanming's office.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lushan's rebellion was greater than the disorders of Li and Pi, and Yi's duty of integrity and investigation was more urgent than Xuanming's office.

sentences.zh: 分命所系，不啻保姆；

translations.literal: The charge entrusted to him was no less than that of a nurse;
translations.idiomatic: The charge entrusted to him was no less than that of a nurse;

sentences.zh: 逆黨兵威，烈於水火。

translations.literal: the rebel forces were more violent than fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: the rebel forces were more violent than fire and water.

sentences.zh: 於斯時也，能與執干戈者同其戮力，挽之不來，推之不去，全操白刃之下，孰與夫懷安偷生者同其風？

translations.literal: At such a time, to exert the same strength as those who wielded weapons, unable to be pulled away or pushed aside, holding firm beneath naked blades — how does that compare in spirit with those who clung to ease and clung to life?
translations.idiomatic: At such a time, to exert the same strength as those who wielded weapons, unable to be pulled away or pushed aside, holding firm beneath naked blades — how does that compare in spirit with those who clung to ease and clung to life?

sentences.zh: 請謚曰貞烈。」

translations.literal: I request the posthumous name Upright and Steadfast."
translations.idiomatic: I request the posthumous name Upright and Steadfast."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was approved.

sentences.zh: 子杞，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Qi has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 杞子元輔。

translations.literal: Qi's son was Yuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's son was Yuanfu.

sentences.zh: 元輔字子望，少以清行聞。

translations.literal: Yuanfu, styled Ziwang, was known from youth for his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu, styled Ziwang, was known from youth for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 擢進士，補崇文校書郎。

translations.literal: The man passed the Jinshi examination and was appointed Proofreader of the Chongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Jinshi examination and was appointed Proofreader of the Chongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 杞死，德宗念之不忘，拜元輔左拾遺。

translations.literal: When Qi died, Dezong could not forget him and appointed Yuanfu Left Reminder of the Missing.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi died, Dezong could not forget him and appointed Yuanfu Left Reminder of the Missing.

sentences.zh: 歷杭、常、絳三州刺史，課當最，召授吏部郎中，進累兵部侍郎，為華州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: The man served successively as Prefect of Hang, Chang, and Jiang Prefectures; his performance ranked highest; he was summoned and appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel, then promoted repeatedly to Vice Minister of War, made Prefect of Hua, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Prefect of Hang, Chang, and Jiang Prefectures; his performance ranked highest; he was summoned and appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel, then promoted repeatedly to Vice Minister of War, made Prefect of Hua, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 元輔端靜介正，能紹其祖，故歷顯劇，而人不以杞之惡為累雲。

translations.literal: Yuanfu was upright, quiet, and principled, and was able to continue his grandfather's legacy; therefore he held prominent and demanding posts, yet people did not hold Qi's wickedness against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu was upright, quiet, and principled, and was able to continue his grandfather's legacy; therefore he held prominent and demanding posts, yet people did not hold Qi's wickedness against him.

sentences.zh: 張介然者，猗氏人，本名六朗。

translations.literal: Zhang Jieran was from Yishi; his original name was Liulang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jieran was a native of Yishi; his original name was Liulang.

sentences.zh: 性慎願，長計畫。

translations.literal: By nature he was cautious and prudent, and skilled in long-term planning.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was cautious and prudent, and skilled in long-term planning.

sentences.zh: 始為河、隴支郡太守。

translations.literal: The man first served as Prefect of a subordinate commandery in the He-Long region.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as Prefect of a subordinate commandery in the He-Long region.

sentences.zh: 王忠嗣、皇甫惟明、哥舒翰踵領節度，並署營田、支度等使。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongsi, Huangfu Weiming, and Geshu Han successively held military commissions and all appointed him to the posts of Camp Fields and Logistics Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongsi, Huangfu Weiming, and Geshu Han successively held military commissions and all appointed him to the posts of Camp Fields and Logistics Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入奏稱旨，賜與良渥。

translations.literal: When he entered court to report, his words pleased the Emperor and he was granted rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered court to report, his words pleased the Emperor and he was granted rich rewards.

sentences.zh: 介然啟曰：「臣位三品，當給棨戟。

translations.literal: Jieran stepped forward and said: "Your servant holds third rank and should be granted halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Jieran stepped forward and said: "Your servant holds third rank and should be granted halberds.

sentences.zh: 若列於京師，雖富貴，不為鄉人知，願得列戟故里。」

translations.literal: If they were displayed in the capital, though I would be rich and honored, my fellow townsmen would not know of it; I wish to have halberds displayed in my native place."
translations.idiomatic: If they were displayed in the capital, though I would be rich and honored, my fellow townsmen would not know of it; I wish to have halberds displayed in my native place."

sentences.zh: 玄宗許之，別賜戟京師第門，仍賜絹五百匹，宴閭里長老。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong granted this, separately bestowed halberds at the gate of his capital residence, and also granted five hundred bolts of silk and held a feast for the elders of his village.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong granted this, separately bestowed halberds at the gate of his capital residence, and also granted five hundred bolts of silk and held a feast for the elders of his village.

sentences.zh: 本鄉得列戟，自介然始。

translations.literal: The custom of displaying halberds in one's native village began with Jieran.
translations.idiomatic: Displaying halberds in one's native village began with Jieran.

sentences.zh: 翰薦為少府監，歷衛尉卿。

translations.literal: Han recommended him as Vice Director of the Palace Workshop; he later served as Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Han recommended him as Vice Director of the Palace Workshop; he later served as Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，授河南節度采訪使，守陳留。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, Jieran was appointed Investigation Commissioner and Military Commissioner of Henan and defended Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled, Jieran was appointed Investigation Commissioner and Military Commissioner of Henan and defended Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 陳留據水陸劇，居民孳夥，而太平久，不知戰。

translations.literal: Chenliu lay at a strategic junction of waterways and roads and its population was large; yet peace had lasted so long that the people knew nothing of war.
translations.idiomatic: Chenliu lay at a strategic junction of waterways and roads and its population was large; yet peace had lasted so long that the people knew nothing of war.

sentences.zh: 介然到屯不三日，賊已度河。

translations.literal: Less than three days after Jieran arrived at his camp, the rebels had already crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Less than three days after Jieran arrived at his camp, the rebels had already crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 車騎蹂騰，煙塵漫數十里，日為奪色。

translations.literal: Chariots and horsemen trampled and churned; dust and smoke spread for several tens of li, darkening the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Chariots and horsemen trampled and churned; dust and smoke spread for several tens of li, darkening the sun.

sentences.zh: 士聞鉦鼓聲，皆褫氣不能授甲。

translations.literal: When the soldiers heard the drums and gongs, their spirits collapsed and they could not don their armor.
translations.idiomatic: When the soldiers heard the drums and gongs, their spirits collapsed and they could not don their armor.

sentences.zh: 凡旬六日，城陷。

translations.literal: Altogether, on the sixteenth day, the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: In all, on the sixteenth day the city fell.

sentences.zh: 初，有詔購賊首而暴誅慶宗狀。

translations.literal: Previously there had been an edict offering a reward for the rebel leader's head and publicly executing Qingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Previously there had been an edict offering a reward for the rebel leader's head and publicly executing Qingzong.

sentences.zh: 祿山入陳留，見詔書，拊膺大哭曰：「我何罪！

translations.literal: When Lushan entered Chenliu and saw the edict, he beat his breast and wept, saying: "What crime have I committed?
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan entered Chenliu and saw the edict, he beat his breast and wept, saying: "What crime have I committed?

sentences.zh: 吾子亦何罪，乃殺之！」

translations.literal: What crime did my son commit, that he was killed!"
translations.idiomatic: What crime did my son commit, that he was killed!"

sentences.zh: 即大恚憤，殺陳留降者萬人以逞，血流成川，斬介然於軍門。

translations.literal: He flew into a great rage and killed ten thousand who had surrendered in Chenliu to vent his anger; blood flowed and formed a river; Jieran was executed before the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: He flew into a great rage and killed ten thousand who had surrendered in Chenliu to vent his anger; blood flowed and formed a river; Jieran was executed before the army gate.

sentences.zh: 以偽將李廷望為節度使，守陳留。

translations.literal: The false general Li Tingwang was made Military Commissioner and left to defend Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: The false general Li Tingwang was made Military Commissioner and left to defend Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 祿山已拔陳留，則鼓而前，無敢亢。

translations.literal: Once Lushan had taken Chenliu, he beat his drums and advanced, and none dared resist.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lushan had taken Chenliu, he beat his drums and advanced, and none dared resist.

sentences.zh: 中宿攻滎陽，太守崔無诐率眾乘城，聞師噪，自隊如雨，無诐與官屬皆死賊手。

translations.literal: The man camped overnight and attacked Xingyang; Prefect Cui Wukou led the masses onto the walls, but when they heard the army's clamor they fell from the ranks like rain; Wukou and his subordinates all died at the rebels' hands.
translations.idiomatic: He camped overnight and attacked Xingyang; Prefect Cui Wukou led the masses onto the walls, but when they heard the army's clamor they fell from the ranks like rain; Wukou and his subordinates all died at the rebels' hands.

sentences.zh: 以偽將武令珣戍焉。

translations.literal: The false general Wu Lingxun was stationed there as garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: The false general Wu Lingxun was left to garrison the place.

sentences.zh: 無诐者，本韋后外家，博陵舊望也。

translations.literal: Wukou was originally from the Empress Wei's maternal clan and came from an old Boling family.
translations.idiomatic: Wukou was originally from the Empress Wei's maternal clan and came from an old Boling family.

sentences.zh: 始，無诐娶蕭至忠女，至忠敗，被貶。

translations.literal: At first Wukou married Xiao Zhizhong's daughter; when Zhizhong fell, he was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wukou married Xiao Zhizhong's daughter; when Zhizhong fell, he was demoted.

sentences.zh: 久乃為益州司馬。

translations.literal: After a long time he became Assistant Administrator of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he became Assistant Administrator of Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 素善楊國忠，既用事，引為少府監，守滎陽。

translations.literal: The man had long been on good terms with Yang Guozhong; once Guozhong took power, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Workshop and made Prefect of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been on good terms with Yang Guozhong; once Guozhong took power, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Workshop and made Prefect of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 有詔贈禮部尚書，謚曰毅勇。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him the title of Minister of Rites and gave him the posthumous name Resolute and Brave.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously granted him the title of Minister of Rites and gave him the posthumous name Resolute and Brave.
